Obama accuses Trump administration of targeting Ilhan Omar
items.description: Former United States President Barack Obama has accused President Donald Trump’s administration of using federal power to intimidate Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar over her criticism of the president. Obama, in a statement posted on his X account on Sunday, condemned the investigation into Omar’s immigration history, describing it as an alarming departure from democratic principles. He said the government should not selectively target individuals because of their political beliefs or public statements. Omar, who represents Minnesota in the US House of Representatives, was born in Somalia and arrived in the United States with her family at the age of 12. She became a naturalised US citizen in 2000 and was elected to Congress in 2018. Obama said Omar had built a career in public service, first as a community organiser and later as a legislator, before becoming one of the Trump administration’s most outspoken critics. He argued that the administration’s scrutiny of her citizenship was politically motivated, pointing to what he described as an unsubstantiated theory that she was older than officially recorded when her father became a naturalised citizen. Federal agents searched Omar’s Washington, DC, residence on October 12 as part of a criminal investigation into possible irregularities in her decades-old immigration paperwork. Authorities also seized her phone, according to reports, while the investigation’s full scope remains unclear. Obama questioned the basis for the investigation, arguing that the federal government was bringing its full weight to bear on an elected official because she had criticised the president. He also cited previous investigations and prosecutions involving individuals viewed as political opponents of Trump, including New York Attorney General Letitia James and former FBI Director James Comey, arguing that such actions raised concerns about the independence of law enforcement. Obama said the investigation could impose significant financial and personal costs on Omar, including legal expenses and time diverted from her responsibilities to constituents. He warned that the use of government institutions to intimidate political critics could have consequences beyond Omar’s case. “The fact that any president, or any administration, is willing to engage in such transparent efforts to intimidate someone should outrage all Americans, regardless of how they feel about Congresswoman Omar’s political views,” Obama said. He cautioned that allowing such practices to become normal could expose other Americans to similar treatment under future administrations, regardless of which political party holds power. Omar has denied wrongdoing and described the search of her home as an attempt to intimidate her. The Justice Department has said the search was authorised by a court warrant and formed part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. The investigation has drawn criticism from Democrats, who have questioned its timing ahead of the November midterm elections. The administration has not publicly established that Omar committed immigration fraud. The post Obama accuses Trump administration of targeting Ilhan Omar appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Prix des viandes importées : Tebboune ordonne des enquêtes
items.description: Le président de la République se penche sur les prix des viandes importées. Au cours d'une réunion du Conseil des ministres qu'il a présidée ce dimanche 18 octobre, Abdelmadjid Tebboune a ordonné l’ouverture d'enquêtes sur les prix appliqués et sur les pratiques de certains importateurs. Tebboune ordonne d'enquêter sur les pratiques de certains importateurs de viande L’État a pris plusieurs mesures pour faire baisser les prix des viandes rouges qui ont flambé sur le marché national. Parmi ces mesures, l'ouverture de l'importation et l’application d’abattements fiscaux et douaniers sur les opérations d’importation. Malgré ces mesures, les prix ne sont pas redevenus accessibles et les viandes importées sont vendues parfois à des prix proches de ceux des viandes locales, à cause de monopoles constitués par certains importateurs. Cette question a été évoquée ce dimanche en Conseil des ministres. Selon un communiqué de la Présidence de la République, repris par le télévision algérienne, le président de la République a ordonné au Premier ministre d’ouvrir une enquête sur “ le rôle néfaste de certains importateurs de viande dans la formation d’un monopole et la hausse des prix pratiqués par les bouchers qui la commercialisent aux mêmes prix que la viande locale ”. Un texte pour réglementer l’activité des intermédiaires Le chef de l'État a aussi chargé le Premier ministre d’ouvrir une enquête sur les écarts de prix de la viande importée entre les wilayas et même entre certains quartiers d’une même ville, ajoute la même source. Abdelmadjid Tebboune a ordonné au cours de la même réunion l’élaboration d’un texte visant à réglementer strictement l’activité des intermédiaires entre les producteurs et les consommateurs. Le président a insisté à plusieurs reprises ces dernières semaines sur la nécessité de combattre la spéculation et les pratiques frauduleuses qui font flamber les prix de certains produits de base. items.title: Lagos cracks down on fake, expired products
items.description: LASCOPA urges consumers to remain vigilant By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has intensified efforts to protect consumers from counterfeit, expired, adulterated and substandard products, warning that premises found violating consumer protection laws risk being sealed. The General Manager of the Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency (LASCOPA), Afolabi Solebo, gave the warning during media appearances on the AskLagos programme aired on Lagos Traffic Radio 96.1 FM and Lagos Television (LTV). Solebo said the agency had continued to identify supermarkets and retail outlets selling unwholesome products, adding that sustained monitoring and enforcement had helped reduce the practice. He said enforcement actions would be publicised to raise public awareness, encourage compliance and deter businesses from violating consumer protection regulations. On price transparency, Solebo urged consumers to report supermarkets and shops that failed to display the prices of goods. He explained that visible price tags enabled consumers to make informed purchasing decisions and helped prevent discrepancies between displayed prices and amounts charged at checkout. Addressing the “No Refund, No Return” policy adopted by some businesses, the LASCOPA boss clarified that blanket disclaimers did not automatically override consumers’ rights to seek redress. He encouraged residents who purchased defective, counterfeit or misrepresented products to lodge complaints with the agency. Solebo also advised consumers to check product labels, verify registration details, examine expiry dates and retain receipts as evidence in the event of disputes. For online transactions, he urged residents to verify sellers, confirm payment terms, use secure payment channels and inspect goods before payment where payment on delivery was available. He urged consumers not to remain silent when their rights were violated but to use the agency’s complaint channels, stressing that effective consumer protection required the collective responsibility of consumers, businesses and regulators. Solebo reiterated LASCOPA’s commitment to protecting consumers’ interests, promoting fair business practices and ensuring a safe and transparent marketplace. Residents can report complaints through LASCOPA’s social media platforms on Facebook, Instagram and X via @lasgcopa, by email at lasgcopa@gmail.com, or through its toll-free helpline, 080 0005 2726. The post Lagos cracks down on fake, expired products appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘It felt like a fresh start’ — Carrick reacts to Man United’s draw at Leeds
items.description: Michael Carrick said Manchester United’s hard-fought 1-1 draw at bitter rivals Leeds on Sunday felt like a “fresh start” even though their long wait for a win goes on. Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo’s first-half opener at Elland Road, extending United’s winless run to six matches in all competitions. But Carrick saw positive signs five days after the 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid, which sparked Lisandro Martinez’s criticism of the club hierarchy over a lack of summer investment. “We’re not getting too carried away because we haven’t won the game,” said the Red Devils boss, who started the Argentina defender at Leeds but had to replace him at the break due to a thigh problem. “I think if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons then you get what you deserve in the end. “It felt like a bit of a fresh start, if I’m honest, today in where we’re at and accepting it and doing something about it. “It definitely shows that the boys are desperate to do well for each other as much as anything else and how much they appreciate playing for this football club, because there was a real purpose to the group over the last couple of days.” United head to Como on Wednesday looking for a first victory since last month’s Champions League opener against Sabah before attempting to kickstart their Premier League campaign at home to Bournemouth. The Red Devils, in 13th spot, have their fewest wins at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986/87. “We’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch,” said the under-pressure Carrick. “I’m realistic with that. “But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of where you have to find a way through it.” He added: “I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve got no doubts that we can go on a good run.” The post ‘It felt like a fresh start’ — Carrick reacts to Man United’s draw at Leeds appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cameroun : Hemley Boum, « Nos vies sauvages » raconte un pays sous emprise
items.description: Que fait un pouvoir qui dure plus de quatre décennies à un pays et à ses habitants ? Dans son nouveau roman Nos vies sauvages, paru chez Gallimard, l'écrivaine camerounaise Hemley Boum raconte les destins de femmes confrontées à la corruption, à la répression et aux compromissions politiques. Un roman qui résonne avec l'histoire du Cameroun, de ses luttes pour l'indépendance à la présidentielle contestée de 2025. Sur France 24, Hemley Boum revient sur le système politique camerounais, la responsabilité des élites, les espoirs démocratiques déçus et les perspectives d'un changement après Paul Biya.

items.title: HURIWA tackles Oyedele over Tinubu’s re-election prospects
items.description: By Chioma Obinna The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has criticised the Minister of State for Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, over comments on President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects, urging the Federal Government to prioritise economic relief for Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement on Sunday, the association’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, said the government should focus on addressing rising living costs, high petrol prices, declining purchasing power and widespread economic hardship rather than discussing the President’s chances of securing a second term. HURIWA faulted what it described as Oyedele’s preoccupation with Tinubu’s electoral prospects, arguing that Nigerians needed concrete explanations of how the administration intended to ease financial pressures on households and stimulate economic activity. The association also questioned suggestions that international investors and financial markets were anticipating Tinubu’s victory in 2027, maintaining that the election outcome would ultimately be determined by Nigerian voters. It said investor sentiment and economic projections should not be treated as substitutes for measurable improvements in citizens’ living conditions. The group challenged the minister to explain the government’s plans to improve workers’ purchasing power, create jobs, strengthen productive sectors and make essential goods and services more affordable. HURIWA also raised concerns about the country’s borrowing profile, arguing that increased government revenue should be accompanied by greater transparency in public spending, stronger fiscal discipline and closer scrutiny of loan commitments. Citing concerns raised by economic commentator Dele Oye in a report published by The Guardian on May 25, 2026, the association called on the government to provide details of its borrowing decisions, including the purposes of loans, the projects they finance and the benefits they deliver. It warned that borrowing without measurable improvements in public welfare could leave future generations with a heavy financial burden. On the removal of the petrol subsidy, HURIWA challenged the argument that subsidies were inherently incompatible with economic development, saying carefully designed public interventions could help protect vulnerable households from economic shocks. The association argued that corruption, waste and weak oversight should be addressed in the design and implementation of subsidy programmes, rather than dismissing public support measures outright. It maintained that the removal of the petrol subsidy, without adequate safeguards for low-income households, had compounded economic hardship as transportation and food costs continued to put pressure on household incomes. HURIWA also cited a report published by TheCable on October 16, 2026, quoting Professor Pat Utomi as criticising the government’s handling of petrol prices and wages. Utomi was quoted as saying: “But does the President care? How does he even sleep at night, knowing that millions of Nigerians are struggling to survive in a country blessed with abundant natural resources?” The association said the remarks reflected public frustration over the contrast between Nigeria’s natural resource wealth and the economic difficulties confronting many citizens. It argued that public support for economic reforms would be difficult to sustain if Nigerians continued to bear their costs without experiencing corresponding improvements in their living conditions. The group urged the Federal Government to prioritise measures to reduce living costs, expand employment opportunities, strengthen purchasing power, tackle corruption and ensure that public revenue translated into tangible benefits for citizens. It also called for transparent fiscal management and targeted relief measures to protect vulnerable households while preventing the misuse of public funds. HURIWA maintained that the performance of the administration’s economic policies should be assessed by their impact on citizens’ welfare rather than investors’ expectations about Tinubu’s re-election prospects. The association urged the government to demonstrate greater sensitivity to the economic difficulties facing Nigerians and show how its policies would improve access to basic necessities. The post HURIWA tackles Oyedele over Tinubu’s re-election prospects appeared first on Vanguard News .

2027: Iyabo Obasanjo urges voters to look beyond party labels
items.description: By Adesina Wahab Senator Iyabo Obasanjo, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Ogun Central, has urged voters to assess political candidates based on their records, commitment to public service and ability to improve people’s lives rather than party affiliation alone. Obasanjo made the call during a television interview with TVC, where she discussed her return to active politics after a 14-to-15-year break during which she pursued an academic career. The former senator also spoke about her political journey, her return to the PDP and her ambition to represent Ogun Central in the Senate in the 2027 general elections. Asked about her party’s preferred presidential candidate for the 2027 election, Obasanjo declined to make an explicit endorsement, explaining that doing so could confuse voters assessing her own senatorial candidacy. Her response highlighted the distinction between the presidential and senatorial contests, with Obasanjo urging voters to consider candidates on their individual merits. Explaining her decision to return to politics after more than a decade away from elective office, the professor of epidemiology recalled a meeting with about 30 community members who urged her to resume public service. She said the group members were not relatives but individuals who had independently decided to appeal for her return. According to her, their sincerity and accounts of how her previous interventions had improved their lives made a strong impression on her and prompted her to reconsider her decision to remain outside elective politics. Obasanjo said the encounter reinforced her belief that her previous work in public office had made a lasting impact on some constituents who believed she could still contribute to their welfare. On what she intended to do differently if elected again, she said her approach to public service remained guided by the same values that informed her previous political engagements and academic career. She explained that her focus had consistently been on helping people improve their circumstances and contributing to the development of society. The former senator cited her previous interventions in the health sector, including grant management and hospital renovation projects, as examples of her efforts to deliver practical benefits to communities. Obasanjo also explained the political developments that preceded her return to the PDP. She recalled that she joined the All Progressives Congress (APC) when she sought the party’s governorship ticket in Ogun State, despite having previously served as a senator on the PDP platform. She said she congratulated the winner of the APC’s consensus process, after which she returned to the PDP to pursue her former senatorial seat in Ogun Central. Obasanjo maintained that her political choices had not altered her underlying commitment to public service, arguing that improving people’s lives remained her central motivation regardless of the party platform through which she pursued that goal. The 2027 elections will provide voters in Ogun Central an opportunity to assess Obasanjo and other candidates based on their records, policy positions and plans for the constituency, alongside their party affiliations. items.title: Kebbi Govt disputes UNDP poverty rating, faults ADC
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Government has disputed a reported poverty rating attributed to the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), describing it as outdated and accusing opposition politicians of using it to criticise the administration of Governor Nasir Idris. The state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed Birnin Kebbi, stated this on Sunday at a press conference held at the Government House in Birnin Kebbi. He claimed that the report being cited covered data from 2018, during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari, and alleged that former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, had brought it to public attention to discredit the Idris administration. The commissioner, however, did not provide details of the report or documentary evidence to substantiate his claims in the information made available. He urged opposition politicians, including those in the African Democratic Congress (ADC), to focus on proposals for the state’s development rather than what he described as efforts to discredit the government. Birnin Kebbi also appealed to residents not to be swayed by what he called politically motivated claims ahead of the forthcoming general elections. He said the Idris administration had made progress in addressing economic challenges and poverty in the state since assuming office three years ago. The commissioner attributed the economic difficulties inherited by the current administration to what he described as a period of economic dislocation and widespread poverty, but did not provide comparative data to support the government’s assessment. On insecurity, he said the state government had supported security operations through the provision of patrol vehicles and logistics, as well as the establishment of military bases in communities considered vulnerable to attacks by armed groups. He also accused Malami of failing to show sufficient concern for communities affected by insecurity during his time in public office, alleging that the former minister had not visited some affected towns to sympathise with victims. Birnin Kebbi further criticised Malami’s comments on insecurity, arguing that his record in public office should be considered when assessing his criticisms of the current administration. The commissioner also made allegations concerning Malami’s conduct while in office, but no supporting evidence was provided in the statement made available for this report. The claims against Malami and the opposition’s position on the poverty rating were not independently verified. The UNDP report cited by the state government’s critics was not provided for review, and the organisation’s position on the dispute was not available. items.title: Karaté : deux médailles de bronze pour le Sénégal aux Mondiaux
items.description: Le Sénégal a décroché deux médailles de bronze aux Championnats du monde de karaté cadets, juniors et U21, disputés à Bielsko-Biała, en Pologne. Mouhamadou Moustapha Cissé et Serigne Mbacké Seck se sont chacun hissés sur la troisième marche du podium dans leur catégorie respective. Mouhamadou Moustapha Cissé a remporté la médaille de bronze en kumité juniors masculins, dans la catégorie des plus de 76 kg. Le Sénégalais a pris le dessus sur le Croate Soltić sur le score de 2 à 1, s’assurant ainsi une place sur le podium mondial. De son côté, Serigne Mbacké Seck a également décroché le bronze en kumité masculin des moins de 21 ans, dans la catégorie des moins de 84 kg. Ouverts mercredi, les Championnats du monde de karaté cadets, juniors et U21 ont pris fin ce dimanche en Pologne. Le Sénégal termine la compétition avec deux médailles de bronze, grâce aux performances de ses deux représentants.

items.title: France in Shock After Protests Turn Into Riots, Damaging Buildings and Shops
Manifestations du 17 octobre: la France va mal!
items.description: Le 17 octobre 2026 avait été annoncé comme une journée de manifestations à travers toute la France. Elle était, dans cette logique, fortement redoutée par les populations. Sauf que les saccages et pillages ne se sont pas limités au samedi, mais ont continué ce dimanche 18 octobre, mettant en exergue, s’il en fallait encore la confirmation, la profondeur de la crise socio-politique que traverse la France. Voici, en quelques chiffres, une journée bien houleuse: 800 000 manifestants, selon les organisateurs du mouvement, et selon la comptabilité du ministère de l’intérieur, 550 000, dont 110 000 dans la seule ville de Paris, pour un mort côté manifestants, suite à «un arrêt cardiorespiratoire», a constaté la préfecture de la capitale. Plus de 2000 interpellations. Des transports en commun, comme le métro, bloqués ou tournant au ralenti. Des hôtels de ville saccagés et incendiés. La résidence d’un préfet attaquée. Et, de nombreux commerces, dont des enseignes de marques, mis à sac. Une note bien salée pour les commerçants, mais surtout pour l’Etat dont des bâtiments symboles, comme des mairies, ont été dévastés ou brûlés. Le bilan est loin d’être exhaustif, mais donne, tout de même, la preuve que la France va mal. Tout a commencé par des revendications de lycéens qui se plaignent du «parcours-sup» et de mauvaises conditions d’études. Tout s’est poursuivi par une grogne sociale portées par plusieurs syndicats et les «gilets jaunes». Et tout a fini par un chaos indescriptible, créé par des casseurs et pilleurs qui semblaient très bien organisés pour tirer le maximum de profit de cette marche, annoncée pacifique et qui se déroulait comme tel à ses débuts. Incompréhension, consternation, sidération et colère. Un chapelet de sentiments mêlés d’amertume, de tristesse et parfois de rancœur, qui pourrait s’égrener à satiété, face aux scènes de violences et de pillages inouïes qui ne peuvent s’imaginer, non pas à Paris, la «ville lumière», mais que dans un scénario de western où les desperados assiègent une ville qu’ils laissent derrière eux, à feu et à sang. Une guérilla urbaine, s’est d’ailleurs installée entre la police et les manifestants, et a duré toute une soirée et même tard dans la nuit et qui a tourné à l’avantage des pilleurs et des vandales du pire acabit. Et pourtant, cette journée apocalyptique du 17 octobre s’est passée dans une France, pays qui, selon l’histoire, il y a des siècles déjà, a apporté la civilisation à l’Afrique. Elle a même exporté vers le continent noir, la démocratie, qui se définit par le gouvernement du peuple par le peuple. Et c’est cette même démocratie qui a permis, dans cette même France, des manifestations qui ont débouché sur des débordements, dont le bilan, qui ne cesse d’évoluer, est catastrophique, pour l’Etat, mais surtout pour de nombreux commerçants qui ont tout perdu dans cette folie collective de casseurs que rien ne semblait pouvoir arrêter! Pas même la police n’a pu contenir, à temps, la vague ravageuse. Alors que c’est de cette police des «blancs» que le professionnalisme en matière de maintien de l’ordre, est tant vanté auprès des Africains! Question: pourquoi les forces de l’ordre ont-elles été incapables de ramener promptement…l’ordre en mettant fin, rapidement, à la furie destructrice des casseurs et voleurs? En attendant que le ministre en charge de l’Intérieur, dont certains, parmi lesquels le Rassemblement National (RN), réclament la tête, donne les raisons de la réaction tardive de ses éléments, ceux-ci ont déjà reconnu qu’ils ont été débordés face à la horde rageuse d’«assaillants». Questions: quelle sera la suite des événements, après le chaos de ce week-end, surtout qu’une autre manifestation est prévue le 5 novembre prochain par des lycéens et des syndicats solidaires de leur lutte? Quelle leçon la France peut-elle encore donner aux Africains, alors que, de plus en plus, l’évidence est établie que trop de démocratie peut tuer la démocratie? Par Wakat Séra L’article Manifestations du 17 octobre: la France va mal! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Kidnapped Catholic Priest, three others rescued in Benue
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A Catholic priest, Rev. Fr. John Otache, abducted along the Otobi Amejo–Ajegbe Road in Ohimini Local Government Area of Benue State, has been rescued alongside three other kidnap victims by a joint team of security personnel and community vigilantes. Otache, the parish priest of St. Margaret’s Parish, Ajegbe-Awume, was kidnapped on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, while travelling home from Otukpo. The victims were reportedly rescued at about 4pm on Sunday after days of operations by security personnel and local vigilantes to secure their release. Local sources said three other persons abducted by armed men along the same route were also freed during the operation. One of the sources, who confirmed the development, said the victims had been taken to hospital for medical attention. “The priest and three other persons were rescued today at about 4pm by a team of local vigilantes and the police, who have been working on the matter in the last few days,” the source said. “It was a successful operation. The victims have been taken to hospital for medical attention. We are, however, hopeful that the priest and the others are in good health,” the source added. The source expressed relief over the rescue but urged security agencies to sustain patrols along the route, which has reportedly experienced repeated kidnapping incidents. The abduction had raised concern among members of the Catholic Diocese of Otukpo and residents of communities along the Otobi Amejo–Ajegbe corridor. Confirming the rescue, the Benue State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, said other victims were also freed during the operation. “Apart from the priest, others were also rescued today during the operation,” he said. items.title: PCB allows Rizwan, Imam to play domestic cricket tournament
items.description: LAHORE/KARACHI: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), apparently taking a step back quietly, has allowed former captain Mohammad Rizwan and opener Imamul Haq to represent their respective teams in the seventh round of the President’s Trophy Grade-I first-class tournament starting on Monday. Both Rizwan and Imam — who represent the Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and the Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) respectively, in domestic cricket — had been under investigation by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) for alleged betting and gambling activities following Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test in England earlier this year. The pair, whose mobile phones were confiscated by the NCCIA, and five other players of the squad in England were withdrawn before the third and final Test which the tourists lost 3-0. According to some reports, both Rizwan and Imam are facing allegations under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). Amid the probe, Rizwan was denied permission to feature in the eight-team President’s Trophy, which started last month. At the time, it was explained away as the player’s failure to appear in a pre-season fitness test. But it later emerged that he had been denied the go-ahead to play because of the NCCIA probe. Though the PCB itself did not issue any official statement on the participation of any of the above-mentioned players, SNGPL coach and former Pakistan captain Mohammad Hafeez has said on electronic media that if available Rizwan would lead SNGPL in the next President’s Trophy match. Hafeez’s statement indicates that there is no bar on Rizwan anymore and now it is up to the wicket-keeper/batsman’s own availability to lead the team. It has been reported that Rizwan had asked the PCB for the no-objection certificate to play the Nepal League, but the PCB only allowed him to feature in domestic cricket. Meanwhile, Imam’s return to the domestic cricket was made official by the OGDCL. Farah Batool, president of the OGDCL sports department, told Dawn that Imam would play the seventh-round match of the President’s Trophy after receiving the directions from the PCB. Sources in the PCB also confirmed this. Rizwan was summoned by the NCCIA in Lahore on Oct 2 when the agency grilled him for more than three hours. However, no official statement on the matter has been released by the NCCIA so far. Rizwan, after this case emerged, had requested the PCB to allow him to use the National Cricket Academy which was denied.

items.title: South-East needs no apology to lead Nigeria — Onoh
items.description: By Emma Nnadozie Former South-East campaign spokesman for President Bola Tinubu, Denge Josef Onoh, has faulted the claim that Peter Obi and the Obidient movement constitute the biggest obstacles to an Igbo presidency, insisting that the South-East does not need to apologise for its political choices or seek permission to aspire to national leadership. Onoh, who is also chairman of the Forum of Former Members of the Enugu State House of Assembly, stated this in a statement made available to journalists in Lagos in response to comments by the convener of The Alternative, Segun Sowunmi, on the Selah Meditate Podcast. Sowunmi had reportedly argued that the South-East was isolating itself through political hostility, tribalism and a failure to negotiate power strategically across Nigeria’s diverse political landscape. But Onoh described the argument as a flawed assessment of the country’s political realities, saying it unfairly placed responsibility for the challenges surrounding an Igbo presidency on Obi and his supporters. He argued that the outcome of the 2023 presidential election contradicted the suggestion that the Obidient movement was confined to the South-East or driven solely by ethnic considerations. “Peter Obi did not run a regional or ethnic campaign,” Onoh said, citing the support Obi received outside the South-East, including in Lagos, Nasarawa, Plateau and the Federal Capital Territory. He described the support as evidence that the movement had attracted Nigerians from different regions and backgrounds. Onoh also faulted what he described as the selective criticism of the Obidient movement over the conduct of some of its supporters on social media. He said passionate political exchanges were common across the major political camps in Nigeria and argued that supporters of one political movement should not be singled out for criticism. According to him, although some political exchanges may be aggressive, they should not be used to deny a region the opportunity to pursue national leadership. Onoh further argued that Obi could not reasonably be expected to control every statement made by supporters of a decentralised, citizen-led movement. He said holding Obi personally responsible for the online conduct of millions of independent supporters would impose an unrealistic standard not consistently applied to other political leaders. On Sowunmi’s reported comments about Igbo businesspeople and their grievances over Nigeria’s economic conditions, Onoh said commercial success did not diminish their right to demand good governance and equitable political representation. “An ethnic group’s resilience, entrepreneurial drive and ability to survive in a hostile economy do not strip them of the right to demand good governance,” he said. He added that the economic contributions of Igbo businesspeople in cities such as Lagos and Abuja should not be treated as a substitute for political representation at the highest levels of government. Onoh maintained that negotiations for political power should not require the South-East to suppress its democratic choices or apologise for supporting candidates it believes can lead the country. “The South-East does not need a permission slip from political actors who are stuck in old ways of doing things,” he said. He argued that the 2023 election had demonstrated the possibility of building political alliances across ethnic and religious lines, adding that the support Obi received should be viewed as a basis for broader national engagement rather than an obstacle to an Igbo presidency. Onoh said the South-East should be able to pursue national leadership through elections, competence and alliances with Nigerians from other regions. His response comes amid continuing debate over the South-East’s political strategy and its prospects of producing Nigeria’s president. items.title: Banks’ profitability moderates, but record GH¢9.2bn profit in 8 months of 2026
items.description: The banking industry remained profitable at the end of August 2026, although profitability moderated compared with the corresponding period in 2025. Profit-after-tax (PAT) declined marginally to GH¢9.2 billion from GH¢9.7 billion a year earlier. This represented a contraction of 5.7%, compared with growth of 46.1% recorded in August 2025. Similarly, profit-before-tax (PBT) contracted by 5.7% on a year-on-year basis, in contrast to the 42.0% growth recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. According to the October 2026 Banking Sector Development Report, growth across the banking industry’s major income lines moderated during the review period, except for fees and commissions income, which increased by 17.9% in August 2026. This is compared with 13.1% a year earlier. In contrast, net interest income contracted by 4.2%, reversing the 21.8% growth recorded in August 2025, largely reflecting the low-interest-rate environment and its dampening effect on interest earnings. Similarly, the growth in other income slowed relative to the corresponding period in 2025. The growth in the banking industry’s cost base moderated during the review period, with operating expenses increasing by 6.4% in August 2026, down from 19.5% a year earlier. The moderation reflected slower growth in staff costs and a contraction in non-staff expenses. In contrast, provisions for depreciation, bad debts and impairment losses rose sharply by 76.3%, reversing the 46.0% contraction recorded in August 2025. Return on Assets and Return on Equity The profitability indicators for the banking sector moderated in August 2026, reflecting the slowdown in earnings growth during the review period. The industry’s Return on Equity (ROE) declined to 22.2% in August 2026 from 32.2% in August 2025. Similarly, Return on Assets (ROA) decreased to 4.3% from 5.6% over the same period. I nterest Margin and Spread Interest spread for the industry narrowed to 5.9% in August 2026 from 7.9% in August 2025. The decrease in spread resulted from the marginal decline in interest payable to 2.2%, from 3.8% a year earlier. Gross yields also declined to 8.1% in August 2026 compared to 11.6% a year ago. The ratio of gross income to total assets (asset utilisation) also dropped to 7.3% from 9.2%, whereas the profitability ratio also recorded a marginal decline to 25.3% in August 2026 from 25.4% in August 2025.

items.title: ONU : Macky Sall se retire de la course au secrétariat général
items.description: L'ancien président sénégalais Macky Sall a annoncé retirer sa candidature au poste de secrétaire général de l'ONU, au lendemain d'un premier vote indicatif de l'instance où aucun candidat n'a fait consensus. Dans une déclaration publiée sur ses réseaux sociaux, Sall dit prendre cette décision en « espérant contribuer ainsi à l'émergence d'une candidature consensuelle au sein du Conseil de sécurité ». « Les résultats des différents votes tests indiquent un choix en faveur d'une candidature issue de la région d'Amérique Latine et des Caraïbes et éventuellement féminine », a-t-il ajouté. Jusqu'à présent, la Costaricaine Rebeca Grynspan, 70 ans, qui dirigeait l'agence de l'ONU pour le Commerce et le Développement (Cnuced), faisait la course en tête. Mais vendredi, aucun des sept candidats en lice n'a réussi à échapper à un vote négatif de l'une des cinq grandes puissances siégeant au Conseil de sécurité (Grande-Bretagne, France, États-Unis, Chine et Russie), ce qui ouvre la porte à d'éventuelles nouvelles candidatures. Derrière Grynspan, arrive l'actuel dirigeant de l'Agence internationale de l'énergie atomique (AIEA), l'Argentin Rafael Grossi, 65 ans, puis Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, 53 ans, ancienne ministre des Affaires étrangères du Guyana. Les autres candidats, sont l'Ougandais Olara Otunnu et les Équatoriennes Maria Fernanda Espinosa, et Ivonne A-Baki. A tout moment, un nouveau postulant peut se déclarer. Ce processus intervient alors que l'ONU traverse l'une des périodes les plus difficiles de son histoire, le multilatéralisme qu'elle défend étant largement mis à mal par des pays qui jusqu'alors le défendaient, comme les États-Unis. Elle est également confrontée à une multiplication des conflits dans le monde et de graves difficultés financières. « Alors que le monde reste confronté à la multiplication des conflits, à l'aggravation des rivalités géopolitiques, à la fragmentation de l'ordre international et à des défis économiques et financiers sans précédent, je demeure convaincu que les Nations unies doivent engager une transformation profonde de leurs méthodes de travail et de leur fonctionnement », a commenté Macky Sall. The post ONU : Macky Sall se retire de la course au secrétariat général appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: LDC CAF : le Horoya AC bat Al Merrikh SC et prend une option avant le retour
items.description: Le Horoya AC a pris une courte mais précieuse avance face à Al Merrikh SC en s’imposant (1-0), ce dimanche 18 octobre 2026, au stade du 28 septembre de Conakry. Cette victoire permet au champion de Guinée d’aborder avec un léger avantage le match retour du deuxième tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions africaine. Devant son public, le Horoya AC a livré une prestation convaincante face au club soudanais d’Al Merrikh SC. Les Rouge et Blanc ont affiché une bonne maîtrise du jeu durant le temps réglementaire, en imposant leur rythme et en contrôlant les débats. Dominateurs, les hommes de Nouhoum Diané ont su gérer leur rencontre sans véritablement se mettre en danger. Cette maîtrise leur a permis de s’imposer sur la plus petite des marges, décrochant ainsi un succès important dans cette double confrontation continentale. L’unique de la rencontre a été inscrit par Yacouba Gnagna Barry juste avant la pause (45è). Toutefois, malgré cette victoire à domicile, le Horoya AC devra confirmer lors de la manche retour pour espérer intégrer la phase de groupes. Le match retour est prévu dans une semaine au Rwanda, où Al Merrikh SC reçoit ses adversaires pour ses rencontres à domicile. items.title: Macron condemns “shocking” scenes of violence across France
items.description: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned on Sunday what he called the “dissenters” who looted ​and vandalised cities in “shocking” scenes across France ‌on the sidelines of protests over the cost of living. “Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: ​what was going through their minds? How ​can French people do this to France?”, Macron said in a televised address to the ​nation. “Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses ​it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame.” Macron, whose final six months in office are being shaped by ​mounting political, fiscal, and social pressures, said he ​had ordered a review to determine whether there had been ‌failings ⁠in intelligence gathering or police preparedness before protests that were later marred by looting and violence. He said prefects and mayors would be empowered ​to ban certain ​gatherings where ⁠necessary. Macron also said he had asked the government to bring together ​students, teachers, lawmakers, trade union representatives and ​business ⁠leaders this week to formulate what he described as “concrete proposals” to address the crisis, without providing ⁠further ​details. “We must sit around the ​table and build solutions together,” he said. items.title: Makinde warns successors against dismantling Oyo agencies
items.description: …Says rule of law, security bodies key to investment, growth By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has challenged his successors to sustain institutions established by his administration, warning that dismantling them could undermine efforts to strengthen governance, maintain public order and drive the state’s long-term development. Makinde spoke at the weekend during the commissioning of the new office complex of the Oyo State Rule of Law Enforcement Authority (OYRLEA), where he said the sustainability of the institutions would be a major test of his successors’ commitment to good governance. He maintained that the agencies established since he assumed office in 2019 were designed to serve the state beyond his tenure and should not be abolished without justification. Among the institutions he listed were OYRLEA; the Oyo State Security Network Agency, known as Amotekun; the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency (OYSADA); the Oyo State Project Performance Monitoring Agency; the Oyo State Mobilisation Agency for Socioeconomic Development (OYMASED); and the Oyo State Anti-Corruption Agency (OYACA). According to the governor, administrations genuinely committed to Oyo State’s progress should sustain the agencies rather than seek to dismantle them. “At the heart of good governance is the rule of law. When people know their rights and security agencies enforce the law without bias, you have order, investors come in, and the economy improves. That is what we have experienced in Oyo State,” Makinde said. He said his administration’s legacy should be measured not only by infrastructure projects but also by the institutions established to promote continuity, stability and accountability in governance. Makinde added that he expected the agencies to remain relevant after his tenure, describing their establishment as part of a deliberate effort to build structures capable of supporting the state’s development over the long term. The governor also commended OYRLEA Chairperson, Justice Aderonke Aderemi (retd.), for her commitment to the Authority’s mandate, saying he had no regrets appointing her despite disagreements they had encountered at certain points. The event featured the commissioning of the Authority’s new office complex and the unveiling of its maiden magazine, which its leadership described as significant milestones in its operations. In his goodwill message, Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Adebo Ogundoyin, said the legislation establishing OYRLEA reflected the Assembly’s determination to provide legal frameworks for addressing practical challenges confronting the state. Ogundoyin said the Authority was responsible for enforcing laws relating to environmental protection, sanitation, waste control, road traffic management, open rearing and grazing, among other matters. He described the responsibilities as important to public order and development, urging the Authority to discharge its duties transparently and responsibly. The Speaker also called on residents, community leaders, business owners, motorists, traders and other stakeholders to cooperate with OYRLEA in enforcing the relevant laws. Earlier, Aderemi described the commissioning of the office complex and the unveiling of the maiden magazine as important steps towards strengthening the agency’s institutional capacity. She said OYRLEA had intensified enforcement of the Oyo State Open Rearing and Grazing Regulation Law through monitoring, public enlightenment and collaboration with traditional institutions, local governments, security agencies and other stakeholders. According to her, the approach is aimed at promoting peaceful coexistence among farmers, herders and other members of the public. Aderemi commended Makinde for supporting the Authority and the state House of Assembly for providing the legislative foundation for its establishment. The ceremony was attended by Deputy Governor Abdulraheem Bayo Lawal; former Chief Judge of Oyo State, Justice Badejoko Adeniji; President of the Customary Court of Appeal, Justice Tajudeen Abdulganiyu; Secretary to the State Government, Professor Musibau Babatunde; Chief of Staff, Bashorun Akinwale Akinwole; Head of Service, Dr Adenike Fashina; Deputy Chief of Staff, Kazeem Adeniyi; Senior Executive Assistant to the Governor, Chief Bayo Lawal; and Chairman of the Association of Local Government Chairmen, Sikiru Sanda. Also present were commissioners, members of the Oyo State Elders’ Council and Advisory Council, service commanders, religious leaders, traditional rulers and other dignitaries. items.title: Taiwo Godwin’s Death: NANS demands independent probe, rejects protest
items.description: By Joseph Erunke The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Ogun State Joint Campus Council (JCC), has demanded an independent investigation into the death of Taiwo Godwin, a student of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Aro, Abeokuta, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the incident must be transparently established. The council, however, distanced itself from a planned protest over the death, warning that individuals organising demonstrations in its name without the authorisation of its recognised leadership did not represent its position. The development comes as the management of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Aro, announced an investigation into Godwin’s death, which occurred while he was receiving treatment at the hospital’s General Medical Practice Unit. In a statement signed by its chairman, Comrade Habeebullahi Adekunle Tijani, NANS Ogun JCC urged the institution’s Students’ Union and other recognised student bodies to engage the hospital management in dialogue to seek clarification and present their demands. The council said the immediate priority should be to establish the facts surrounding the death, ensure accountability and prevent the incident from generating unnecessary tension. It also called on the hospital management to demonstrate openness by allowing student representatives to express their concerns and obtain answers to questions surrounding the incident. According to Tijani, a transparent investigation supported by constructive engagement between students and hospital authorities would help resolve outstanding questions and restore confidence among students and other stakeholders. NANS warns against exploitation While demanding accountability, the council cautioned against attempts by individuals or groups to exploit the tragedy for personal gain, warning that the incident must not become a pretext for extortion, intimidation or the pursuit of selfish interests. “For the avoidance of doubt, NANS Ogun State JCC is not planning or authorising any protest over this incident. Any individuals or groups organising or threatening protests in the name of NANS Ogun JCC without the authorisation of its recognised leadership do not represent the Council or its position,” the statement said. The council urged security agencies to remain vigilant and take lawful action against anyone attempting to exploit the incident to foment disorder, extort money or threaten peace and security in Ogun State. It maintained that a meeting involving the Students’ Union, other recognised student unions and the hospital management was necessary to address concerns surrounding Godwin’s death. Tijani said the hospital authorities must be willing to listen to the students, respond to their demands and work towards a satisfactory resolution. “Students must be heard, accountability must be pursued, and the peace of Ogun State must be protected,” the council stated. Hospital begins investigation Meanwhile, the management of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Aro, Abeokuta, has confirmed that an investigation into Godwin’s death is underway. In a statement issued on Saturday, the hospital expressed sadness over the incident and assured students, staff members and the public that the circumstances surrounding the death would be examined in accordance with established procedures. The statement, signed by the hospital’s Public Relations Officer, Abiola Ajibola, on behalf of the Acting Provost and Medical Director, said the management was committed to ensuring that the investigation was thorough, impartial and transparent. It added that steps were being taken to expedite the process and establish the facts surrounding the incident. “We further assure all concerned that every necessary step will be taken to establish the facts, address any issues identified, and ensure that justice is served,” the statement read. The investigation is expected to clarify the circumstances surrounding Godwin’s death, as NANS Ogun JCC insists that dialogue, transparency and accountability should guide the response to the incident. items.title: Indian actor Tiger Shroff remains unhurt in shooting incident in Mumbai
items.description: Indian actor Tiger Shroff remained unhurt in a shooting incident in Mumbai’s Juhu area, in which his driver and a bystander sustained injuries, local media reported. A report by Indian news website The Hindu quoted an official as saying that the incident took place around 7pm as Shroff was leaving his place of work. Mumbai Zone-II Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg further said that Shroff’s driver, Firdaus, sustained an injury to his left hand while a bystander, identified as Chauhan, was also wounded and taken to a hospital. According to the report, Maharashtra Chief Minister and Home Minister Devendra Fadnavis has directed Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti to investigate the case and take action against the perpetrators. Meanwhile, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde told The Hindu that “our priority is to keep Mumbai’s citizens safe. We will not spare anyone trying to threaten our film industry”. He added, “It is time we respond to them in their own language. In the 1990s, Mumbai saw the gang war era. The Mumbai Police stopped it. We will not tolerate such gangs. This incident is unfortunate.” The All Indian Cine Workers Association, which represents those part of the film industry, released a statement on the incident, saying it was “shocked and deeply anguished by the firing on Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area”. “This is not an isolated incident. Shots were fired outside Salman Khan’s residence in Bandra. Actor Saif Ali Khan was stabbed in an attack at his Bandra home. Shots were fired outside the Juhu home of filmmaker Rohit Shetty. Comedian Kapil Sharma’s cafe was attacked repeatedly. Now Tiger Shroff has been fired upon. “One after another, people from the film industry are being targeted, and a deliberate atmosphere of fear is being created. The intent is plain: gangsters want to terrorise Bollywood personalities and extort money from them,” the statement said. The association said that despite repeated incidents, the government and the police had failed to stop these attacks. “Gangsters have openly claimed responsibility in earlier cases, yet the network continues to operate. Statements are not enough. Bollywood needs real protection,” it stressed. It demanded from CM Fadnavis to take the strictest possible action against the gangsters behind these attacks, arrest the shooters and also those who ordered the firing, without delay, and “break the extortion network”. The body also called for provide adequate security and protection to film personalities and their families and fix accountability for the repeated failure to prevent these attacks. Local media reported that the responsibility of the attack was claimed in an unverified social media post, which said: “Those in the Mumbai industry who work with Salman Khan and don’t listen to us will meet the same fate.” Authorities have not addressed the post yet.

items.title: Moulay El Hassan remet les trophées du Grand Prix Roi Mohammed VI de saut d’obstacles
items.description: Le Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan a présidé, dimanche après-midi au Parc d'expositions Mohammed VI d’El Jadida, la cérémonie de remise du Grand Prix Roi Mohammed VI de saut d’obstacles. Ce prestigieux événement est l’épreuve phare du calendrier équestre national, organisé dans le cadre de la finale de la 15e édition du Morocco Royal Tour CSI 5*W, dont la dernière étape est disputée à l’occasion de la 17e édition du Salon du Cheval, placée sous le haut patronage du Roi Mohammed VI. A son arrivée au Parc d’expositions Mohammed VI, le Prince Héritier a été accueilli par Moulay Abdellah Alaoui, Président de l’Association du Salon du Cheval, avant de passer en revue un détachement de la Garde Royale qui rendait les honneurs. Il a été ensuite salué par le ministre de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et de la Souveraineté alimentaire, Khalid Hatimy, le ministre de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et des Sports, Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid, le Président du Comité national olympique marocain, Fayçal Laâraichi, le wali de la région de Casablanca-Settat, gouverneur de la préfecture de Casablanca, Mohamed Mhidia, le président du Conseil de la région, Abdellatif Maâzouz, et le gouverneur de la province d’El Jadida, Sidi Saleh Daha. Moulay El Hassan a aussi été salué par le président du conseil provincial d'El Jadida, la présidente de la commune de Haouzia, ainsi que par les membres du conseil d'administration de l'Association du Salon du Cheval. Par la suite, il a rejoint la carrière A du Parc d’Expositions Mohammed VI et pris place à la tribune d’honneur d’où il a assisté à la deuxième manche de la finale du Grand Prix Roi Mohammed VI, remportée par le cavalier belge Jérôme Guery montant Kiliman Sitte, au terme de deux manches ayant connu la participation de 44 cavaliers originaires de 16 pays, à savoir le Maroc, la France, l’Allemagne, la Belgique, les Pays Bas, l’Arabie Saoudite, l’Italie, le Brésil, la Suisse, l’Espagne, la Grèce, la Colombie, le Portugal, l’Irlande, la Grande Bretagne et Monaco. Au terme de cette compétition, organisée par la Fondation Morocco Royal Tour dans le cadre de l'agenda sportif de la Fédération équestre internationale, Moulay El Hassan a remis le Grand Prix Roi Mohammed VI au vainqueur. Il a également remis les Prix aux quatre cavaliers ayant occupé les places suivantes au classement, à savoir la Britannique Chloe Aston montant Akito Von Rocherath Z, le Français Simon Delestre montant Golden Boy DK, l’Allemand Tom Schewe montant Congress Blue PS, et l’Italien Roberto Previtali montant Quirinus 27. Moulay El Hassan a, par la suite, posé pour une photo-souvenir avec les cavaliers primés. Le Morocco Royal Tour est un événement incontournable du calendrier équestre international. En effet, il s’agit d’un circuit international de saut d’obstacles qui se déroule, en trois étapes dans trois villes différentes : Tétouan (du 01 au 04 octobre), Rabat (du 07 au 11 octobre) et El Jadida (du 15 au 18 octobre). L’étape d’El Jadida marque une évolution majeure avec l’accession du concours au niveau CSI5*W, le plus haut niveau de compétition internationale en saut d’obstacles et qualificatif pour la Coupe du Monde. Cette progression s’inscrit dans la continuité de la montée en gamme qui a marqué cette édition, avec le passage du CSI1* au CSI2*, amorcé dès la première étape à Tétouan et poursuivi lors de la deuxième étape à Rabat. L’étape d’El Jadida constitue ainsi l’aboutissement de cette évolution sportive et technique, illustrant l’ambition du Morocco Royal Tour d’élever le niveau des compétitions, de renforcer le rayonnement international du circuit et d’offrir aux cavaliers davantage d’opportunités de concourir au plus haut niveau. The post Moulay El Hassan remet les trophées du Grand Prix Roi Mohammed VI de saut d’obstacles appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Man, son burnt to death in Jos tricycle crash
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — A man and his son were reportedly burnt to death after a commercial tricycle, popularly known as Keke NAPEP, caught fire following a road crash in the Sabon Barki area of Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State on Sunday. Three other persons sustained injuries in the incident, which occurred at about 4:20 p.m. as the family was reportedly returning from church. An eyewitness, Kefas Gyang, said the tricycle was allegedly hit by a bus, resulting in the crash and subsequent fire. Gyang said the man’s wife sustained a broken leg, while two other children and the tricycle operator were taken to hospital for treatment. Recounting the incident, the eyewitness said he was returning from work when he noticed people crying and moved closer to ascertain what had happened. “I was passing by on my way from work when I saw people crying and I went closer to find out what had happened and saw people trying to rescue the victims,” he said. “But the fire was too much for us to handle. It was beyond our strength, and we could not do much to rescue them from the burning tricycle.” Gyang said the man and his son were burnt beyond recognition in the fire, adding that he did not witness the actual collision. “When the other vehicle hit the Keke, I was not there. I only came across the scene afterwards and saw people crying,” he said. He further alleged that the driver of the other vehicle fled the scene after the crash. Efforts to reach the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) for comments on the incident were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. items.title: Atiku tackles Tinubu over Police Exit Bill
items.description: …says serving officers dip into pensions By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain his delay in acting on the Police Exit Bill, alleging that serving police officers are dipping into their pension savings to feed their families while retired personnel struggle to survive on meagre stipends. Atiku said the plight of serving and retired officers demanded urgent action on police welfare, including a salary review and resolution of the pension concerns raised by retirees, following the pay increase approved for members of the Armed Forces. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, on October 18, Atiku recounted cases of retired officers allegedly living on inadequate pensions, searching for menial jobs and begging for alms after decades of service. “Men and women who answered Nigeria’s call for decades are now waiting outside its legislature for Nigeria to answer theirs. Bola Tinubu should be ashamed that it has come to this,” he said. Atiku cited the case of a retired Assistant Superintendent of Police who allegedly receives a monthly pension of ₦29,000 and told him that more than 120 members of his association had died in the past three years. He also recounted how a retired Assistant Commissioner of Police allegedly resorted to begging at the Central Mosque in Abuja after failing to find work. “No former officer should have to be discovered in distress before Nigeria remembers what it owes her,” Atiku said. In another account, he said a retired officer in Bauchi had resorted to gathering firewood for sale to afford food, while some serving policemen had allegedly withdrawn 25 per cent of their pension savings to meet their families’ needs. “We ask them to risk their lives for Nigeria while they wonder how to feed their families and whether their country will stand by them when their service ends. That is a disgrace,” he said. Turning to the Police Exit Bill, Atiku said the legislation was sent to Tinubu in March but that the President had yet to make his position known as of October. Citing Section 58 of the Constitution, he said the President had a 30-day period to signify assent or withhold it from a bill presented for assent, and demanded an explanation for the delay. “Bola, a bill gathering dust cannot buy food or medicine. Tell Nigerians what you have done with it,” he said. Atiku urged the National Assembly to publish the bill’s formal status, demand an explanation for the delay and determine the constitutional steps available to resolve the matter. He also pledged that, if elected president in 2027, he would introduce a Police Dignity Guarantee Plan to settle verified pension arrears and gratuity claims, establish a pension floor, provide healthcare coverage for serving and retired officers, and ensure timely support for families of personnel killed in service. The proposed plan, he said, would also include a police salary review, clearer records of pension contributions and entitlements, and published payment schedules to improve accountability. “We will provide for the Guarantee in the budget and publish what has been paid,” he said. items.title: Tinubu campaign council begins nationwide tour of traditional rulers
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress APC Presidential Campaign Council has begun a nationwide tour of traditional rulers ahead of the 2027 general elections, starting with the Emir of Ilorin and the Ooni of Ife. The Director General of the Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, led a delegation of party chieftains to the Emir of Ilorin, Alhaji (Dr.) Ibrahim Kolapo Sulu-Gambari, in Kwara State. The delegation also called on the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi (Ojaja II), in Osun State. A statement issued by Yari’s media office on Sunday night said the visits were meant to deepen the party’s engagement with traditional institutions and to seek the counsel and support of the royal fathers. It added that the Council was not asking the monarchs for an endorsement or for help in mobilising voters. According to the statement, the delegation came “but rather to seek the prayers and blessings of the royal fathers, underscoring the moral and spiritual anchorage traditional rulers provide in the nation’s political process.” The statement said the two visits “mark the formal commencement of a nationwide consultative tour to traditional and political leaders across the country, building consensus and gathering blessings ahead of key campaign activities leading up to 16th January 2027, a significant date in the electoral calendar.” Speaking at the Emir of Ilorin’s palace, Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State, said he was confident the APC would win the presidential, governorship, National Assembly and State House of Assembly seats in Kwara. He pointed to progress recorded in the state since 2019, including the resolution of past challenges in education and healthcare delivery, the establishment of new hospitals and wide-ranging reforms. Yari said the campaign would draw on the strength of the party and the achievements of the Kwara State Governor, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq. He added that the Governor’s role as Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum would help the party extend its reach nationally. The statement said the consultations reflect the Council’s recognition of the part traditional rulers play in promoting peace, unity and stability. It also said the party remains committed to carrying all stakeholders along in the build-up to the elections. Yari was accompanied by the National Secretary of the APC, Senator Ajibola Bashiru; a former Governor of Kano State, Dr. Abdullahi Umar Ganduje; and a former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Honourable Aminu Bello Masari. Also on the delegation were Senators Adamu Aliero, Ali Modu Sheriff, Rochas Okorocha, Ahmad Sani Yarima, Mohammed Badaru Abubakar and Danjuma Goje. They are former governors of Kebbi, Borno, Imo, Zamfara, Jigawa and Gombe states respectively. The team also included two other former governors, Ibrahim Shema of Katsina State and Olusegun Mimiko of Ondo State, as well as another former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Honourable Dimeji Bankole. items.title: AbdulRazaq commends Wike’s inclusion in Presidential Campaign Council
items.description: ..Says APC/PDP in Kwara Is 70-30 By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq has commended the inclusion of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, in the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, saying the development would boost President Bola Tinubu’s re-election chances in the state. AbdulRazaq said Kwara remained a stronghold of the APC, claiming that the party enjoyed a 70 per cent to 30 per cent advantage over the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) since the 2019 general elections. The governor spoke on Sunday in Ilorin while receiving a delegation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, led by its Director-General, Senator Abdulazeez Yari. He said Wike’s inclusion in the council, alongside his reported support for Tinubu’s re-election, would further strengthen the ruling party’s position in the state. “We appreciate this courtesy visit. It’s important to know, to hit the ground running, you’re going to campaign, and to know that Kwara is solidly in the APC’s side of defence,” the governor said. “The leader of PDP made our job much easier. The balance of the equation here is 70-30. 70 per cent APC and 30 per cent PDP. And that’s consistent from 2019 until the election. Nothing has changed except that PDP has continued to weaken.” AbdulRazaq added that Wike’s reported declaration of support for Tinubu would further consolidate the APC’s position. “With the national leader of PDP being a member of our (APC) campaign council and declaring that his party, the PDP, will vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it means that the PDP 30 per cent versus our 70 per cent is now adding up to 100 per cent. “So, this will be one of the easiest states for our party, because the two main parties in the state are voting for President Tinubu,” he said. The governor commended the composition of the campaign council, describing its members as experienced politicians whose contributions to nation-building had earned them places in the party’s campaign structure. He praised the delegation for commencing its nationwide engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying its early mobilisation demonstrated seriousness and commitment to the task. “I congratulate you for being nominated into PCC, the highest organ of our campaign. It’s because the party recognises your capacities, your contribution to nation-building and what you can achieve,” he said. The delegation included several former governors and former members of the National Assembly, among them Aminu Bello Masari, Rochas Okorocha, Ali Modu Sheriff, Adamu Aliero, Abubakar Badaru, Danjuma Goje, Ibrahim Shema, Sani Yerima, Abdullahi Ganduje and Olusegun Mimiko, as well as former House of Representatives Speaker Dimeji Bankole and Olubunmi Ette. The visit also featured the Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly and APC governorship candidate, Salihu Yakubu Danladi; his running mate, Seun Oguniyi Adato; and state APC chairman, Prince Sunday Fagbemi, alongside other government officials. AbdulRazaq highlights achievements The governor also highlighted his administration’s achievements in addressing infrastructure deficits and improving education, healthcare and civil service welfare. He cited the introduction of KwaraLEARN, a technology-driven teaching programme in public basic schools, saying it had helped reduce absenteeism and improve learning outcomes. AbdulRazaq recalled that when his administration assumed office in 2019, the state faced challenges involving unpaid salaries, pensions and gratuities, but said those problems had been addressed. “When we came in 2019, it was a challenging situation. Salaries were not paid, gratuities were not paid, pensions were not paid. That is a thing of the past. The civil servants are happy with us now. The people are happy with us. They can see measurable progress,” he said. He also expressed confidence in Danladi’s emergence as the APC governorship candidate, describing him as a grassroots politician familiar with the administration’s programmes and the workings of government. According to the governor, Danladi’s experience as Speaker of the State Assembly would support continuity, given his familiarity with the state budget, government policies and legislative oversight. He added that the party’s deputy governorship candidate was also a member of the State House of Assembly, saying both candidates were familiar with the state’s political landscape. Yari seeks continued support Earlier, Yari said the delegation visited Kwara to appreciate AbdulRazaq’s contributions to the APC and seek his continued support for the party’s nationwide campaign. He thanked the governor for the reception accorded the delegation on arrival at the General Tunde Idiagbon International Airport, Ilorin, describing it as an exceptional show of hospitality during the council’s tour. “Your Excellency, we are here to pay homage. We know, particularly I personally know what you are doing to ensure that APC succeeds not only in Kwara but also in Nigeria,” Yari said. He acknowledged the governor’s role in advising Tinubu and the campaign council, assuring him of continued cooperation. The delegation also paid homage to the Emir of Ilorin and Chairman of the Kwara State Council of Chiefs, Dr Ibrahim Sulu-Gambari, seeking his prayers and blessings for the APC and its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. At the palace, Yari praised Tinubu’s administration and AbdulRazaq’s leadership in Kwara, urging the traditional ruler to support the president’s re-election bid. The Emir thanked the delegation for the visit and prayed for the success of Tinubu and all APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. “You are all going to be victorious, and I wish you success in your future endeavours, In Sha Allah,” Sulu-Gambari said. items.title: Keur Massar : une randonnée du Conseil départemental pour promouvoir l’excellence scolaire
items.description: Le Conseil départemental de Keur Massar a organisé ce dimanche 18 octobre 2026 une grande randonnée pédestre départementale. Pensée comme une mise en jambes de la 4ᵉ édition de la Journée de l’Excellence, l’activité a réuni sport, santé, sensibilisation et mobilisation citoyenne. Elle s’est achevée au Lycée de Malika, où se tiendra la cérémonie, désormais fixée au 5 décembre prochain. Les rues du département de Keur Massar ont pris des allures de grand rassemblement populaire. À l’initiative du Conseil départemental, et en collaboration avec la Fédération des Randonneurs du Sénégal, des marcheurs de tous âges ont pris part à une randonnée pédestre départementale placée sous le signe du sport, de la santé et de la cohésion sociale. Partie de Keur Massar Nord, la caravane a rallié le Lycée de Malika, point de chute de la marche et futur cadre de la Journée de l’Excellence. Le choix de ce parcours n’est pas anodin : il relie symboliquement l’effort physique à la réussite scolaire, conformément au thème retenu pour cette quatrième édition, « Éducation et sport : les clés de l’excellence ». Avec cette randonnée, le Conseil départemental, présidé par le Professeur Babacar Guèye, entend élargir la célébration du mérite scolaire à une approche plus globale de l’excellence. Selon la collectivité, la réussite des jeunes repose autant sur la performance académique que sur la discipline, la persévérance, la santé et le bien-être, des valeurs que porte la pratique sportive.L’activité a également permis de faire sortir la Journée de l’Excellence du seul cadre scolaire, en associant les populations du département à la dynamique autour de l’événement. Au-delà de la promotion de l’activité physique, la randonnée a servi de tribune de sensibilisation sur la lutte contre la traite des personnes. Les organisateurs ont appelé à une mobilisation collective et à une vigilance accrue face à ce fléau. L’arrivée à Malika a été l’occasion d’annoncer officiellement la date de la 4ᵉ édition de la Journée de l’Excellence. Initialement envisagée pour le 21 octobre, elle se tiendra finalement le samedi 5 décembre 2026 au Lycée de Malika. Ce rendez-vous doit permettre de récompenser les meilleurs élèves du département ayant brillé aux examens et concours nationaux, de valoriser leurs performances et d’encourager la culture de l’excellence chez l’ensemble des élèves. Lors des éditions précédentes, quelque 500 élèves du département avaient été primés et avaient reçu du matériel didactique, informatique et des fournitures scolaires. C.T.N

items.title: LDC CAF/ Horoya AC : Nouhoum Diané satisfait de la victoire, mais critique le contenu du match
items.description: Le Horoya AC a pris une courte avance face à Al Merrikh SC du Soudan (1-0), lors du match aller du deuxième tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions de la CAF. Malgré ce succès à domicile, l’entraîneur des Rouge et Blanc, Nouhoum Diané, n’a pas caché son insatisfaction quant à la prestation de ses joueurs. Le match retour est prévu le 24 octobre au Rwanda. Mais pour Nouhoum Diané, cette victoire ne suffit pas à effacer les insuffisances observées dans le jeu de son équipe. En conférence de presse d’après-match, le technicien guinéen a reconnu l’importance des trois points obtenus, tout en pointant les lacunes de ses joueurs, notamment dans la finition. « Oui, je suis satisfait parce qu’on a les trois points. Mais par rapport au contenu, non. Je ne suis pas du tout satisfait », a-t-il déclaré. Sur le plan offensif, le coach du Horoya estime que son équipe aurait pu se mettre à l’abri avant le déplacement au Rwanda. Selon lui, plusieurs occasions auraient dû permettre aux siens d’inscrire deux ou trois buts. « On pouvait marquer deux ou trois buts sur ce match », a regretté Nouhoum Diané, qui attend davantage d’efficacité de ses attaquants. Au-delà du manque de réalisme, l’entraîneur a également relevé des difficultés dans l’entrejeu. Le technicien s’est également exprimé sur le positionnement de certains éléments, notamment dans l’organisation défensive et au milieu. Il estime que l’adaptation à différents postes fait partie des exigences du football de haut niveau. Malgré les insuffisances relevées, Nouhoum Diané retient l’importance de cette victoire avant le match retour, prévu le 24 octobre au Rwanda. Il reste toutefois prudent sur les chances de qualification du Horoya AC face à un adversaire qu’il considère comme une équipe de référence sur le continent. « Je vais au Rwanda pour tout mettre en œuvre afin que le Horoya puisse se qualifier », a-t-il assuré.
