items.title: Final day: Republic Bank-JoyNews Habitat Fair clinic in Ho closes on a high note with fun, big sales
items.description: The Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair clinic in Ho has ended on a high note, with lively activities, exciting offers and strong sales marking the final day of the three-day event. Held at the Ho Sports Stadium, the fair brought together businesses in the housing and real estate sector, offering prospective homeowners and property investors the opportunity to explore products and services to support their housing needs. Exhibitors offered discounts of up to 30% on selected products and services, attracting patrons looking for affordable deals on housing-related purchases. The exhibition featured a range of offerings, including building materials, home appliances, property development services and real estate financing options. The final day provided visitors with an opportunity to engage directly with exhibitors, compare prices and explore available solutions, while businesses used the platform to showcase their products, connect with potential customers and boost sales. Beyond the commercial activity, the fair offered an engaging atmosphere for patrons, combining business opportunities with fun as visitors explored the various exhibition stands. Organised by JoyNews and sponsored by Republic Bank, the Habitat Fair seeks to connect consumers with businesses and service providers across Ghana’s housing and real estate industry. The Ho edition also formed part of efforts to extend the fair beyond Accra and other major urban centres, bringing housing solutions and property-related services closer to prospective buyers in the Volta Region and surrounding communities. The event’s conclusion marks another opportunity for exhibitors to reach new customers while helping patrons make informed decisions about homeownership, construction and property investment.

items.title: Goudiry : les populations marchent pour réclamer des ralentisseurs sur la RN1
items.description: Des jeunes, des femmes et des enfants ont battu le macadam, samedi 17 octobre 2026, à Goudiry, pour réclamer l’installation de ralentisseurs et le renforcement des mesures de sécurité sur la Route nationale 1 (RN1), après plusieurs accidents mortels sur cet axe traversant la commune. La marche, organisée de manière pacifique et apolitique, fait suite notamment au décès du jeune A. Cissakho, âgé de moins de huit ans, heurté par une ambulance le mercredi 7 octobre, vers 17 heures, alors qu’elle circulait de Tambacounda vers Bakel. Les organisateurs évoquent également la mort du fils d’Ibra Thiam sur la même route. À travers cette mobilisation, les populations souhaitent attirer l’attention des autorités sur les risques liés à la circulation dans la traversée de Goudiry, où la RN1 côtoie des quartiers habités, des établissements scolaires, des structures sanitaires et des services publics. Les manifestants demandent notamment l’installation de ralentisseurs réglementaires, l’aménagement de passages piétons sécurisés, le renforcement de la signalisation et de l’éclairage, ainsi que des contrôles réguliers de vitesse, particulièrement aux heures d’entrée et de sortie des classes. Dans un mémorandum adressé au préfet du département, les organisateurs sollicitent également une visite technique urgente associant les services compétents, la municipalité et les populations. Ils préconisent, en attendant la réalisation des travaux, des mesures provisoires pour mieux protéger les usagers, notamment les élèves et les autres personnes vulnérables. Le document demande par ailleurs la mise en place d’un cadre de concertation sous l’égide du préfet, l’établissement d’un calendrier précis des interventions, la désignation d’un interlocuteur et l’organisation d’une réunion de suivi dans les trente jours suivant la remise du mémorandum. La mobilisation intervient au lendemain d’une mission d’inspection de l’Agence nationale de sécurité routière (ANASER) dans le département. Vendredi 16 octobre, une délégation de l’agence s’est rendue à Goudiry à la suite des sollicitations des populations en faveur de l’installation de ralentisseurs. Elle a également effectué une visite de courtoisie auprès du préfet du département, Alseyni Bangoura. Les organisateurs n’entendent pas préjuger des responsabilités dans les accidents évoqués, mais réclament des mesures préventives pour réduire les risques sur cet axe routier. Leur message résume l’objectif de la mobilisation : « Des ralentisseurs aujourd’hui pour sauver des vies demain ! »

items.title: Route et électricité à Mali : le grand bond en avant d’une ville en pleine modernisation
items.description: Entre l'arrivée récente de l'électricité et les premiers kilomètres de goudron livrés, la commune urbaine de Mali connaît une transformation sans précédent. Si le visage de cette ville de la Moyenne Guinée se modernise au fur et à mesure, le manque d'eau potable et l'attente du grand axe Labé – Mali – Kédougou rappellent qu'il reste encore du chemin à parcourir a constaté sur place la rédaction régionale de votre quotidien électronique Guinéenews. Des rues désenclavées, un éclairage continu et le sentiment palpable d'une ville en pleine mutation. Aujourd’hui, la commune urbaine de Mali ne ressemble plus tout à fait à celle d'hier. Portée par l'arrivée de l'électricité et les premiers travaux de bitumage, la localité opère une métamorphose majeure qui redonne espoir à ses habitants. Comme le veut le dicton, « la route et l’électricité sont les premiers maillons du développement ». À Mali, ce concept n'est plus une promesse, mais une réalité quotidienne. Le maire de la commune urbaine, Mamadou Dian Dieng, ne cache pas sa satisfaction : « C’est déjà un sentiment de soulagement et d’espoir. Nous profitons de l’occasion pour saluer les efforts du gouvernement, qui ne ménage aucun effort pour améliorer les infrastructures, afin d’offrir à nos populations le cadre de vie souhaité. » Sur les 17 kilomètres de bitume prévus pour la voirie urbaine, près de 3 kilomètres ont déjà été posés en 2026. Une première étape encourageante, bien que le chantier ait été temporairement suspendu en raison des fortes pluies. « Même provisoires, ces travaux améliorent déjà l’image de la ville, facilitent la mobilité et renforcent son attractivité. Nous osons espérer que cette dynamique de modernisation va se poursuivre », ajoute le maire. En plus du désenclavement routier, Mali figure parmi les premières préfectures de la région administrative (après Labé) à bénéficier d'un réseau électrique stable et de qualité. Une avancée rendue possible grâce au projet d'interconnexion régionale géré par l'OMVG (Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du fleuve Gambie). « Cela fait maintenant près de trois ans que nous bénéficions du projet d’interconnexion lié au barrage de Sambagalou. Ce réseau relie la Guinée, le Sénégal et d'autres pays membres. Avec des postes installés notamment à Mali, Labé, Linsan ou Kédougou, c'est toute une sous-région qui s'interconnecte », explique Mamadou Dian Dieng. Malgré ces avancées significatives, un point noir persiste : l’accès à l’eau courante. Malgré la présence de la SEG (Société des Eaux de Guinée), la topographie accidentée et le relief de la zone compliquent sérieusement la distribution. « C'est notre grande équation aujourd'hui. Nous n’avons pratiquement pas d’eau, car la distribution est très difficile, en particulier pour les quartiers situés en hauteur », reconnaît amèrement le premier magistrat de la ville. Autre attente majeure des populations : l'aboutissement des travaux de la route nationale Labé – Mali – Kédougou. Alors que le chantier est en cours, les habitants attendent de pied ferme la livraison de cet axe transfrontalier stratégique pour désenclaver définitivement la région.

items.title: Burkina: des boutiques scellées et des marchandises illicites saisies
items.description: (Toula, le 18 octobre 2026) La Direction régionale de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat du Nazinon (DRICA-Nazinon) a mené, ce dimanche, une opération de contrôle des prix et de la qualité des produits de grande consommation à Toula, dans la commune de Manga. Cette intervention a permis d’inspecter huit établissements commerciaux, de mettre deux boutiques sous scellés et de saisir des produits périmés ainsi que des marchandises prohibées. L’opération vise à vérifier le respect de la réglementation commerciale et la conformité des produits proposés aux consommateurs. Les contrôles ont révélé plusieurs manquements aux règles en vigueur, conduisant à la fermeture immédiate de deux boutiques et à la saisie de marchandises illicites. À travers cette intervention, la DRICA-Nazinon réaffirme sa volonté de contribuer à l’assainissement des marchés locaux et à la protection des consommateurs. Elle rappelle aux commerçants leur obligation de respecter la réglementation en vigueur, notamment en matière de commercialisation des produits, et les met en garde contre la vente de denrées impropres à la consommation ou de marchandises interdites, passible de sanctions administratives et judiciaires. La DRICA-Nazinon annonce la poursuite des contrôles inopinés dans l’ensemble de la région afin de veiller au respect des règles commerciales, de préserver la santé publique et de renforcer la protection des consommateurs. DCRP/MICA DRICA/ Nazinon L’article Burkina: des boutiques scellées et des marchandises illicites saisies est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Techiman residents get free health screening as KGL Foundation marks Breast Cancer Awareness Month
items.description: For students who spend more than three months in school before returning home for vacation, staying healthy is not just a personal concern; it is essential to their education. That was the motivation behind an 18-year-old student, Thomas, for participating in a health screening exercise organised by the KGL Foundation in Techiman, where over 200 people, including young people, men and women, benefited from screening services aimed at promoting early detection and preventive healthcare. “This is my first time participating in health screening because we will spend more than three months in school before vacation. We need to be healthy to study in school,” Thomas said. He expressed hope that the exercise would not uncover an illness that could become a hindrance to their education, while urging fellow students to take regular health checks seriously. “Some illnesses cannot be detected with our physical eyes. It will require medical screening, so I encourage every student to participate in health screening,” he added. The health screening, organised during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, offered breast cancer screening alongside checks for blood pressure, human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B and C, and eye conditions, among other services. The outreach was organised by KGL Foundation in collaboration with Koranteng Memorial Clinic and AgricoHub. The initiative sought to encourage early detection of potential health problems while bringing essential screening services closer to residents. Beyond breast cancer awareness Programs Manager of KGL Foundation, Mr. Nii Ankonu Annorbah-Sarpei, said the exercise was designed to promote breast cancer awareness while helping participants assess their general health. “We’re not just covering breast screening; we’re also checking people’s general well-being, specifically ear screening, eye testing, and blood pressure,” Mr. Annorbah-Sarpei said. Mr. Annorbah-Sarpei added that the target audience included the general population, particularly young people and women, while encouraging both men and women to participate in breast screening. Health professionals say such initiatives can help address misconceptions about breast cancer and encourage people to seek medical attention before conditions become more difficult and expensive to manage. Madam Elizabeth Korsah Koranteng, CEO of Koranteng Memorial Clinic, one of the Foundation’s partners for the exercise, stressed that early screening could support timely diagnosis and treatment. “Breast cancer can financially derail you, so it’s important to screen for early detection, diagnosis, and treatment.” She also challenged misconceptions that breast cancer is a curse, emphasising the importance of accurate health information and early medical assessment. Connecting health to livelihoods and education For AgricoHub, the collaboration reflects the relationship between personal wellbeing and economic productivity. CEO of AgricoHub, Mr. George Antwi Boasiako, said business owners must pay attention to their health as they pursue growth. “We believe that while you focus on your business and business growth, it is important to look at your health and wellbeing, which is why we are collaborating with KGL Foundation for the health outreach,” he disclosed. “The idea is that you should be healthy and able to run your business,” Mr. Antwi Boasiako added. One participant in the exercise said regular screening was already part of her personal healthcare routine. “My health is my priority, so I need to screen all the time.” She reiterated that she regularly visits the hospital for checks involving HIV, breast cancer, HPV and hepatitis B. Blood donation exercise Alongside the screening services, the outreach included a blood donation exercise, with a medical expert describing voluntary blood donation as an important contribution to lifesaving medical care, noting that anyone could eventually need a transfusion, either personally or through a friend or family member. “Blood donation is very important because you, yourself, a friend, or a family member may need it.” She added that donated blood could help save lives when patients require transfusions.

items.title: LDC CAF : le Horoya AC s’impose face à Al Merrikh et prend une option avant le retour
items.description: Le Horoya AC de Conakry a battu Al Merrikh SC du Soudan (1-0), ce dimanche 18 octobre 2026, au stade du 28-Septembre de Conakry, lors du match aller du deuxième tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions de la CAF. Yaghouba Gnagna Barry a inscrit l’unique but de la rencontre. Les deux équipes ont eu des occasions en première période. Le club soudanais s’est procuré la première opportunité, mais sa frappe a été contrée par le dispositif défensif du Horoya AC, sous la vigilance du gardien Sékou Salif Sylla. À la 24e minute, Yaghouba Gnagna Barry a manqué l’ouverture du score sur une passe lumineuse de son coéquipier Ismaël Camara. Sa frappe a terminé dans le petit filet. Le champion de Guinée a ensuite accentué la pression sur la défense adverse. Les efforts des Rouge et Blanc ont finalement été récompensés à la 44e minute. Sur un coup franc bien négocié, Yaghouba Gnagna Barry a trouvé le chemin des filets et permis au Horoya AC de prendre l’avantage avant la pause. Au retour des vestiaires, le club de Matam a poursuivi ses offensives pour tenter de creuser l’écart. Malgré plusieurs occasions, les Guinéens n’ont pas réussi à inscrire un deuxième but. Le Horoya AC s’impose ainsi sur la plus petite des marges (1-0) et prend un léger avantage avant le match retour face à Al Merrikh SC.

items.title: CHASS raises concerns over indiscipline in schools, backs sanctions
items.description: The Conference of Heads of Second Cycle Schools (CHASS) has expressed deep concern about the rising cases of indiscipline among students and staff in senior high schools. The association strongly condemned such acts and assured parents and stakeholders of its commitment to ensuring the safety and protection of all students. “We will support any appropriate sanctions meted out to any staff if found culpable, while insisting on a fair and unbiased process,” CHASS said in a communique issued at the end of its 64th Annual National Conference in the Volta Region. The conference was themed: “Student Discipline in a Challenging World: Context, Challenges and a Constructive Way Forward.” The communique was signed by the President of CHASS, Reverend Father Stephen Owusu Sekyere, and the General Secretary, Mr Primus Baro. Delays in release of funds The association said the primary challenge confronting its members was the long delays in the release of insufficient funds, despite the establishment of a dedicated source of funding for the Free SHS policy, which CHASS strongly advocated. “We would no longer accept excuses and explanations of data discrepancies that led to the bitter experience in the 2025/26 academic year where first-year funds were withheld for the whole year. We look forward to the full payment of all arrears, including the legacy arrears of recurrent grant spanning 2021 to 2024 to enable schools clear their longstanding indebtedness to benevolent creditors,” it said. Emergency procurement payments On emergency procurement, CHASS said heads were officially authorised by the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service to urgently procure food items to feed students in November and December 2025. It said the money was yet to be released to pay the suppliers, some of whom were chasing innocent heads for their money. “We request that this is settled without any further delays to relieve Heads of this overwhelming burden,” it said. Upward adjustment of feeding grant The communique said the current rate of GH¢2.85 per student per day for perishable items no longer reflected market realities. The same challenge, it said, applied to all items under the recurrent grant. “We strongly appeal to the Government to upwardly adjust these allocations to align with current economic conditions and to ensure that students are fed with nutritious meals,” it said. On the waiver of VAT on school procurement, CHASS said it was worrying that procurement of perishable food items and other basic academic resources attracted 20 per cent VAT, as insisted by auditors. “We appeal to government to urgently waive such tax since its incidence is burdening the already woefully inadequate funds,” it said. Food procurement policy The heads requested clarity on the government’s policy of decentralised procurement of 40 per cent of essential food items at the school level, as originally proposed, to feed students effectively and impact the local economy. Student tablets and digital safety The communique said the supply of tablets to students without charging units was a threat to the safety of school facilities, since unregulated charging of tablets was a probable cause of the rampant fire outbreaks in schools. “We request immediate supply of the charging units to all schools. We also urge the Ministry of Education to direct the Supplier to deactivate social media functions on the tablets, to ensure they remain strictly dedicated to educational purposes. We further recommend the reintroduction of textbooks to students instead of the reliance on tablets,” it emphasised. Restoration of PTAs CHASS said it had been a year since the government announced the restoration of parent-teacher associations in schools, but legal controversies were affecting their effective operationalisation. It said the longer the impasse prolonged, the more schools and students suffered. “We request that parents/guardians should freely be allowed to exercise their duty of care in the best interest of their wards in the respective schools without let or hindrance,” it said. The association also noted with grave concern the deteriorating security situation in schools and recommended a shift from the outdated watchman system to the deployment of properly trained, well-equipped and educated security personnel. It further requested the urgent recruitment of critical non-teaching staff to fill existing vacancies. Commendations CHASS expressed appreciation to the government for its continuous efforts to advance secondary education and the Free SHS policy. It commended the government for the creation of a dedicated source of funding for the Free SHS policy by uncapping the Ghana Education Trust Fund to make adequate resources available. “We are grateful to the Ministry of Education and the Ghana Education Service for a stable, uninterrupted academic calendar, especially restoring the calendar to the pre-COVID era,” it said. It also commended the publication of a new Scheme of Service that decouples “post” from “rank” in the Ghana Education Service. Minister’s initiative CHASS commended the Minister for Education for convening the National Conference on Stemming the Growing Indiscipline in Schools in July 2026, particularly for the declaration of a zero-tolerance policy on violence, bullying and any criminal conduct in secondary institutions. It acknowledged the government’s effort in securing a World Bank facility of US$300 million to improve infrastructure in schools and end the double-track system by 2028. “We strongly urge government to expedite measures to fully achieve this target through the provision of new facilities, completion of stalled projects and supply of furniture. Transitioning to a unified single-track calendar will significantly lower operational costs, reduce stress on staff and infrastructure, and ensure uninterrupted implementation of the curriculum,” it said. Leadership The communique praised heads of schools for their extraordinary leadership, courage, resilience and sacrifice in managing the schools despite numerous challenges. It also recognised the contributions of teachers, non-teaching staff and other stakeholders. “Finally, CHASS commends the Honourable Minister for Education for the assurances given to resolve challenges confronting Senior High Schools in Ghana, including ending the double track system and ensuring timely and regular release of funds,” it said.

items.title: Adutwum’s spokesperson demands GES Director-General’s accountability over Obuasi SHTS rape cases
items.description: The spokesperson for former Education Minister Dr Yaw Osei Adutwum has called on the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES) to account for the delay in interdicting the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) over reported rape cases. In a statement, Yaw Opoku Mensah questioned why the headmaster’s interdiction came only after ministerial intervention, despite provisions in the GES Code of Conduct that allow for interdiction when an employee’s continued stay at post could interfere with an investigation. He said the matter had remained in the public domain for more than nine weeks before the action was taken, raising concerns about the Service’s handling of the case and the consistency with which its rules were being enforced. “Why did it take a ministerial directive for an action that the GES Code of Conduct already provides a remedy?” he asked. Citing Section 8 of the GES Code of Conduct, Mr Opoku Mensah noted that an employee should be interdicted if they are under investigation and their continued stay at post is likely to interfere with the process. The code also states that interdiction may be justified where the alleged offence could be grave. He argued that these provisions raised questions about why the matter was not addressed promptly, particularly if the circumstances warranted the headmaster’s removal from post during the investigation. Mr Opoku Mensah further accused the GES leadership of creating the perception of selective enforcement of its rules and prioritising political interests over the integrity of the Service. “The Director-General cannot hide behind bureaucratic excuses while public confidence in the Ghana Education Service continues to erode,” he said. He called on the Director-General to explain the delay, account for the decisions taken and demonstrate that the interests of the GES would not be subordinated to political considerations. Mr Opoku Mensah stressed that the protection of the alleged victims and the integrity of the investigation must remain the priority, adding that the Service needed leadership that applied its rules consistently and without fear or favour. He described the Director-General’s handling of the matter as evidence of incompetence and questioned his commitment to protecting the integrity of the GES.

items.title: Parliament puts off vote on authorizing Sisi to send troops to Saudi Arabia until Tuesday
items.description: After a closed session on Sunday that ran for nearly three hours, the House of Representatives postponed a vote on authorizing President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi to send troops on a combat mission to defend Saudi Arabia, putting it off until after Monday’s and Tuesday’s sessions. Sisi had called for an emergency parliamentary session during the Egyptian Military Academy graduation ceremony on Saturday, asking lawmakers to authorize him to take any measures necessary to protect Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks “if we are asked to do so.” The delay came after MPs demanded details of the Armed Forces’ role in Saudi Arabia beyond the National Defense Council’s statement , asking that every MP get a chance to express their views on the matter, according to three lawmakers who spoke to Mada Masr. MP Ehab Mansour, the Egyptian Social Democratic Party parliamentary bloc head, told Mada Masr after the session that members were instructed not to share details of the discussions with the media. “We are not looking for a role to play, but it makes no sense whatsoever for us to allow any harm to come to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, its security or its stability,” Sisi said during the graduation ceremony. He appealed to “everyone in the Gulf” to stop the war. “Regardless of this appeal, whether it is heeded or not, Egypt, in line with His Majesty King Salman and Crown Prince Mohamed bin Salman’s directives, will carry out any measure to protect and defend you,” he added. Sisi stressed that he is not speaking “in order for us to fight anyone or attack anyone. We are speaking only in defense.” Following Sisi’s remarks, House Speaker Hesham Badawy called an emergency plenary session for Sunday morning. Article 152 of the Constitution requires the president to consult the National Defense Council before declaring war or sending armed forces on combat missions outside the country. It also requires approval from two-thirds of the members of the House of Representatives, voting in a closed session under Article 130 of the House’s bylaws. Before Parliament convened, the presidential spokesperson announced three points agreed upon by the National Defense Council at a meeting chaired by Sisi earlier on Sunday morning. The council declared Egypt’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, out of a belief that Saudi national security is tied to Egyptian and Arab national security, and pledged to provide the country with all necessary and available forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources and territorial integrity and safeguard Islamic holy sites. The council also called for continued and intensified political and diplomatic efforts, coordinated with relevant regional and international parties, to de-escalate tensions across the region and peacefully resolve the crisis affecting it. A senior judicial source criticized the wording of the presidential request. “No state takes directives from another state,” he told Mada Masr on condition of anonymity. The source explained that the Constitution requires Parliament’s approval before troops are sent on combat missions outside the country, meaning the president must specify the nature of the mission, its strategic value to the country and the number of soldiers needed to carry it out. That “authorize me and I’ll handle it” matter, the source said, is “unconstitutional.” In a video posted to his personal Facebook account, MP Reda Abdel Salam, an economics professor at Mansoura University, laid out his view of the president’s authorization request, saying he was unable to express it during the session as each MP was allotted only two minutes. “If Egypt takes part in defending Saudi Arabia, it is only defense, with no Egyptian soldier sent onto Yemeni soil and no Egyptian strike or bullet fired at brotherly Yemen,” he said. “We are defending, alongside Saudi Arabia, the property, wealth, vital sites, airports and water and power stations. Egypt’s participation is defensive only, while mediation efforts continue.” An MP with military background who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity expected Egypt’s involvement to be limited to deploying air defense forces and missiles, while also replacing some Saudi units with Egyptian forces and carrying out limited airstrikes against naval targets, without deploying troops in ground combat. The source said that Egypt’s military doctrine since former President Gamal Abdel Nasser’s experience in Yemen has been shaped by the principle that the military “does not kill Arabs with its own hands.” A governmental source echoed this view. “What we will do is send defensive forces to Saudi Arabia and naval forces to the Red Sea,” he said. “That will benefit us in our relations with both Saudi Arabia and Ethiopia , as it sends a very strong message to Ethiopia about our presence in that area.” Similarly, an informed political source explained that the understanding is for the Egyptian military support to be purely defensive and confined to protecting Saudi Arabia. Forces would enter Yemen from the Saudi side only if the Houthis launch a ground invasion, the source said, adding that such action is unlikely as the Houthis lack the capacity to do so. They can send drones, or engage in battles against the Yemeni military, but at the same time, they are under growing pressure on the ground, he added. This official stress on purely defensive aims and on staying out of any offensive, which Sisi’s announcement affirmed and the various sources emphasized, fits the state’s broader stance of avoiding entanglement in regional wars, even when circumstances call for openly supplying military support. This was plain to see when Egypt sent a “ detachment ” — a limited military formation drawn from one or several corps — to the United Arab Emirates in May. Sources at the time said that the word “detachment” came to “signal the limited size of the formation and the limited duration of the presence,” a gesture of Egyptian support for the UAE against Iranian attacks that stopped short of real Egyptian involvement in the war. Egypt has historically had reservations about any ground intervention in Yemen, dating back to the 1962-1967 war, when Nasser sent troops to back the republicans in North Yemen against the Saudi-backed royalists. The intervention began small and grew to around 70,000 soldiers. Estimates of Egyptians killed range from 10,000-26,000. Nasser himself described the war as his own Vietnam, since it drained both the military and the economy, and a large share of the troops were still in Yemen when Egypt was defeated in 1967. The intervention ended with the withdrawal of troops late that year, after Nasser and then- Saudi King Faisal reached an agreement on the sidelines of the Khartoum summit. Since then, a conviction to avoid getting entangled on the ground in Yemen has become ingrained in the military’s memory, something some analysts call the “Yemen complex.” Egypt has previously taken part in the coalition Saudi Arabia has led in Yemen since 2015 under Operation Decisive Storm. It dispatched four naval vessels to secure the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Gulf of Aden, alongside air force participation. Cairo said at the time that it is prepared to send ground troops “if the situation warrants,” but it never did. Ahead of Parliament’s emergency session, the speaker of the Houthi-controlled House of Representatives in Sanaa, Yahya al-Raei, sent Badawy a letter urging him not to be pulled along by the policies of the Saudi regime, warning that “Egypt’s slide down this path would pose a grave danger to its national security and internal stability.” In the letter, of which Mada Masr obtained a copy, Raei wrote, “We categorically reject that the Egypt of Arabism and history be dragged into a battle that does not resemble its values,” adding, “We have always known Egypt as a supporter of Yemen’s unity and stability.” Raei accused the Saudi regime of waging “aggression and a blockade on Yemen for more than 12 years,” of shirking implementation of the roadmap by circumventing understandings and political efforts aimed at peace and of tightening the blockade on the Yemeni people to the point of famine in some areas. He stressed that “the Saudi regime is the one that proceeded to end the de-escalation phase by targeting the Sanaa airport and chose to escalate through air raids on most Yemeni regions, targeting civilian infrastructure.” He also accused it of involvement in backing and financing groups he described as “Takfiri,” including the Islamic State, in their war against the Yemeni people. An Egyptian government official previously told Mada Masr that Egypt has kept an open channel of communication with the Houthis, especially since they took control of Bab al-Mandab in September. The front between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is seeing its most violent escalation since the 2022 truce collapsed. In July, the Houthis declared a “naval blockade” of the kingdom and attacked Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea. In September, they launched a ground attack, capturing the Yemeni Mokha Port, which had been under the control of the Saudi-led coalition’s joint forces, effectively controlling Bab al-Mandab. By early October, the two sides were escalating: the internationally recognized Yemeni government launched the Fajr al-Yemen Operation to retake Sanaa, backed by extensive Saudi air support, while the Houthis attacked facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco and struck King Khalid International Airport, killing 12 people and wounding hundreds. The crisis comes amid shifts in the map of regional alliances. In August, Riyadh signed a joint defense pact with Turkey and Pakistan, in what came to be known as the Mecca Pact. Cairo, a member of the Quad formed by the pact’s signatories, didn’t join. According to diplomats and officials in Cairo who spoke to Mada Masr at the time, Egypt was not willing to sign up for what it saw as a Saudi-authored political bloc that would undermine its own ability to maneuver regionally. On September 10, Axios reported , citing United States officials, that bin Salman called US President Donald Trump twice, urging him to launch strikes against the Houthis, but Trump rejected. The officials said the US administration “does not intend to take direct military action against the Houthis at this time” and that Trump’s directives are to keep US forces focused on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz and to avoid opening another front. Five days later, bin Salman visited Egypt at the head of a delegation that included Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud and Saudi National Security Advisor Musaed al-Aiban. The Saudi Royal Court said the visit was made at the direction of King Salman to discuss ways of strengthening bilateral relations and issues of common interest. On September 20, CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with Sisi in Egypt. Iranian outlets took the visit as feeding speculation that Washington wants to hand Cairo a larger role in regional security arrangements. On Tuesday, Foreign Minister Badr Abdel Atty said Egypt would respond to any Saudi request, and joining the “Mecca treaty” is now “under serious consideration.” Saudi Asharq Bloomberg cited on Friday an official source saying Cairo is negotiating with Riyadh to renew deposits to the Central Bank of Egypt worth US$5.3 billion, which mature this month. According to the source, the talks are focused on how long the renewal should last, with no final agreement yet. The next day, at the Military Academy graduation ceremony, Sisi called on the military parade leader, the Armed Forces’ commanders and the rest of the state officials in attendance to give a military salute to the Gulf states, in appreciation of their economic support for Egypt after “the events of 2011,” as he put it. The post Parliament puts off vote on authorizing Sisi to send troops to Saudi Arabia until Tuesday first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Le gouvernement clarifie les circonstances du limogeage de Madiha Khayr
items.description: Après la polémique suscitée par la nomination de Madiha Khayr au poste de ministre déléguée chargée de la Formation professionnelle et de la Qualification, le porte-parole du gouvernement, Samir Belfkih, a expliqué que la gestion rapide du dossier visait à permettre à l’exécutif d’achever son processus constitutionnel de formation et de recentrer le débat public sur son programme. Dans un communiqué publié ce dimanche 18 octobre, le ministre de l’Aménagement du territoire national, de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de la Politique de la ville, également porte-parole du gouvernement, a indiqué que la réaction rapide de l’exécutif relevait de sa responsabilité politique et institutionnelle. Selon le communiqué, le gouvernement a suivi les développements ayant accompagné la nomination de Madiha Khayr, notamment la circulation d’informations à caractère judiciaire et médical relevant de la vie privée. Les composantes de la majorité ont, à cette occasion, réaffirmé leur volonté commune de faire réussir l’expérience gouvernementale, de recentrer le débat public sur le programme de l’exécutif et les attentes des citoyens, et de servir l’intérêt général. Samir Belfkih a également rappelé que la cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, avait adressé au Roi Mohammed VI une demande de décharge de Madiha Khayr de ses fonctions ministérielles. Cette démarche s’appuie sur les prérogatives constitutionnelles de la cheffe du gouvernement, notamment celles prévues au quatrième alinéa de l’article 47 de la Constitution. Laquelle demande a été acceptée par le Souverain. La décision intervient après le débat médiatique suscité par la nomination de Madiha Khiyer au sein du nouvel exécutif, dont les membres ont été nommés vendredi dernier par le Roi Mohammed VI au Palais royal de Rabat, sous la présidence de Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri. Le nom de Madiha Khayr a fait l’objet d’une large couverture médiatique après la circulation d’un ancien document médical remonteant à 2004. Certaines publications ont établi un lien entre ce document et une ancienne affaire judiciaire. Avant son entrée au gouvernement, Madiha Khayr avait suivi un parcours politique au sein du Parti de l’Istiqlal. Elle avait occupé plusieurs responsabilités dans les instances du parti, avant d’intégrer son comité exécutif en octobre 2024, puis de prendre la tête du groupe istiqlalien de l’unité et de l’égalitarisme à la Chambre des représentants. Pour Samir Belfkih, la rapidité de traitement du dossier doit permettre au gouvernement de poursuivre les étapes nécessaires à son installation constitutionnelle, notamment son investiture parlementaire. L’exécutif entend ensuite se consacrer à la mise en œuvre de son programme et au respect de ses engagements envers les citoyens. Dans son communiqué, le porte-parole insiste sur la volonté des composantes de la majorité de préserver la dynamique de la nouvelle expérience gouvernementale et de replacer le programme gouvernemental au centre du débat public. La priorité affichée est désormais d’achever le processus constitutionnel de formation du gouvernement et d’engager la mise en œuvre des orientations annoncées pour la prochaine étape. items.title: 2,000 arrested as French unrest spills into second day
items.description: French police battled protesters and looters for a second day on Sunday as the country reeled from the violent chaos left by a day of cost-of-living demonstrations in which around 2,000 people were arrested nationwide. Paris city workers had not finished clearing up the torched cars, smashed shopfronts and burnt debris from Saturday’s unrest when the new troubles started and political recriminations erupted. AFP journalists said several hundred people gathered in the Republique square in the capital following social media calls for a gathering that authorities said had not been approved. Television footage showed the looting of a clothing store and bikes were also set alight nearby. The Paris police prefecture said security forces moved in when “faced with the initial signs of tension”. AFP journalists saw police firing tear gas and stun grenades at hundreds of people gathered in the square. Bottles and rocks were hurled at police who made several arrests. Some 550 people out of 855 arrested in Paris remained in detention from Saturday’s troubles and police stations were struggling to cope, according to the Legal Team Paris group of lawyers. Government under pressure Six months from a presidential election, the government faced opposition attacks over preparations for the nationwide day of action that followed weeks of mounting student protests over conditions in schools. President Emmanuel Macron, who on Saturday vowed that anyone who engaged in vandalism or looting would be prosecuted, was to address the nation on Sunday evening at 1800 GMT. Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate for the National Rally party, said the troubles showed that Macron’s administration was “running on fumes, exhausted and disoriented”. “We are experiencing a profound crisis of trust and authority, which poses a threat to democracy,” said Le Pen, who leads opinion polls ahead of the election . Le Pen has blamed ultra-left groups, while Jean-Luc Melenchon head of the far-left France Unbowed party accused authorities of inflaming tensions. With images of French town halls burning and shops being looted grabbing headlines around the world, US President Donald Trump waded into the debate, blaming immigration for the unrest. “France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country,” Trump said in a social media post. Looting rampages were reported on Saturday in Paris and other cities, including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Strasbourg, on the margins of protests over the cost of living. Around 1,500 businesses were damaged with losses estimated at hundreds of millions of dollars, according to the Retail and Trade Federation. One person died during the main march in Paris, but officials said the case was health-related. “It’s like we had a war,” a 78-year-old Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told AFP amid burnt street barricades from the protests. ‘Animals’ Another resident, Anita Gras, said she saw young men loot a sports shoe retailer. “It’s appalling, terrifying — groups of young people came here yesterday, looting, smashing everything, with total impunity,” said 57-year-old Cecile Rogue surveying a pile of charred bicycles. The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire that local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI had been deliberately set by “a wild horde”. About 7,000 people staged a march in the central city on Sunday to show their anger at the devastation. In Lyon, a store owner, Jean-Christian, said those behind the violence were “animals”. “We saw them looting, men high on adrenaline.” A tourist office in the city centre was set ablaze during the protests amid multiple clashes and looting. On Sunday, a clothing store was also looted in Lyon. Tourists stunned In Paris, startled tourists were seen on Saturday running with suitcases along streets filled with tear gas and protesters. A Danish tourist, Soren Petersen, said it was “sad” to see damage to Paris buildings. “It is not a protest, it’s far beyond a normal protest,” he told AFP . Around 500 police, firefighters and paramedics were hurt in the protests, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. The violence took place on the sidelines of nationwide protests that the interior ministry said drew 550,000 people. The CGT union said 800,000 people participated. A 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in the southern city of Saint-Etienne. In Mulhouse a 17-year-old girl lost an eye, according to prosecutors. France’s Yellow Vest movement, which staged street protests eight years ago against Macron’s government over planned fuel-tax hikes, had called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations.

items.title: Bilawal says KP governor's rule could end if opposition engages with Centre on counterterrorism
items.description: PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Sunday that if the opposition was willing to fight against terrorism and engage with the Centre on a plan, governor’s rule and emergency imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa could end. He made these remarks while speaking to the media in Karachi, where he was visiting the Karsaz Monument on the 19th anniversary of the Karsaz bombing . His statement comes a week after the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI, which was in power in KP and in opposition in the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. “If they really want to fight terrorists, and if they want that emergency and governor’s rule in KP to end, they should engage with the federal government and politicians and discuss a united policy regarding the fight against terrorism,” Bilawal said on Sunday, referring to the PTI-led opposition. He added that if the opposition was ready to fight terrorism and “we agree on a plan” to do so, the emergency and governor’s rule in KP could end. “If the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister (Sohail Afridi) is a coward, if he is not ready to defend his homeland, if he is not ready to fight those terrorists, then the PPP is ready to fight them,” Bilawal said. “That is why we supported the government’s decision to impose governor’s rule in KP.” He stressed that the party would “join forces with everyone to fight these terrorists”. In his media talk, the Bhutto scion said the country had reached a point where “terrorist attacks are taking place from Khyber to Khuzdar”. He regretted that when the Taliban came to power in Kabul in 2021, the Pakistani government at that time “also decided to invite the terrorists who were in Afghanistan to come back and live in our Swat, our Malakand, our former tribal areas”. He was seemingly referring to then-prime minister Imran’s plans to resettle members of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan in the country. Bilawal went on to say that terrorists who were in jail in Pakistan were also freed. “Today, Pakistan is suffering the losses from these wrong decisions,” he lamented. He added that the country had now once again reached the point where “some forces want to take down Pakistan’s flag in Swat” and there was a fight against terrorism ongoing across the entire country, while security forces, law enforcers and the public were being targeted. However, he claimed, in the province where the highest number of terrorist incidents were taking place — KP — its chief minister had pledged that he would not face the terrorists. In response to a question about the Karsaz bombing, the PPP chairman remarked that the greatest loss was caused when terrorist incidents were not taken seriously. He said that the PPP had “prepared entire society” to fight terrorism by creating an environment for counterterrorism operations in 2008, when the party was in power. After that, he said, when the National Action Plan was introduced, the PPP adopted a holistic approach towards bringing changes in institutions to assist with combatting terrorism. He emphasised that success was achieved when “every citizen” of Pakistan joined the fight against terrorism, saying, “Today as well, we will make efforts to create an environment where we are all united, and will fight the terrorists together.” Answering further questions, he said Pakistan was facing a “historic economic crisis”. “It appears that the situation will worsen. Our priority is to address this economic crisis, and to do that, we will have to fight terrorism as well,” he added. He said efforts should also be made to improve the democratic and electoral system in Pakistan. For this reason, he said, the PPP had highlighted the need for a new NAP and consensus on the fight against terrorism, while also extending an invitation to the opposition to play a part in this. He said the PPP also made an effort to improve the democratic system by pushing for electoral reforms. To this end, the federal government had decided to establish an electoral reforms committee in the National Assembly, adding that he had invited the opposition to play their part in that committee as well. “If they say that democracy is weak in this country, they should help us to strengthen it,” the PPP chairman said. He added, “If we can create such an environment, we will be in a better position to fight terrorists.” Bilawal also said KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had been nominated by the PPP for the office of governor, but “constitutionally, he is now a representative of the federal government”. He said Kundi reported to the federal government, but “I will keep talking to him and keep advising him; in principle, though, he is now working together with the federal government”. Responding to a question regarding a potential “compromise” with the opposition, Bilawal said, “You say ‘compromise’ like it’s a bad word […] Compromise and politics go hand in hand.” He stressed that ex-PM Benazir had always strived for compromises during her political career, adding that she knew that one could reach “extremes” if they remained a revolutionary or an activist who only protested rather than working for their cause. “We had to solve our issues and lift the public and our workers out of difficulty,” Bilawal said about the PPP’s past tenures in government. He asserted that it was the result of the PPP’s “compromises” that led to the end of Gen Pervez Musharraf’s dictatorship, as well as the passage of the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment. “We (the PPP) are not in the federal government. Nor do we have a majority in Parliament,” he said. “But [we have to see] how we can conduct politics in the space we have.” New provinces Answering a question regarding the creation of new provinces, Bilawal stated that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi knew “clearly” what the PPP and President Asif Ali Zardari’s policy was regarding new provinces or administrative units, and that this was “not possible without the president’s signature”. Naqvi’s July remarks calling for new provinces and reforms in the current governance system had ignited an animated debate across the country. The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any possible division of the province. Bilawal stressed that the PPP’s position was clear: that they could be created in accordance with the Constitution and law if the provincial assembly agreed. The Sindh Assembly, amid a boycott by the opposition, adopted a resolution last month rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units. “Where there is consensus and it is not a political stunt, if there is no other purpose behind it … why aren’t provinces being made there?” the PPP chairman said, giving the example of Gilgit-Baltistan. “If we really want this to be implemented, it must only be implemented where the provinces want this,” he stressed, noting that the entire GB Legislative Assembly had passed a resolution with consensus for the region’s constitutional rights. Bilawal requested politicians, whether on the treasury or opposition benches, not to politicise the issue of terrorism or create controversy out of steps taken to combat it, but rather to play their role in fighting it. Bilawal also spoke about Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, saying he had the right to criticise the government’s policies, and that there should certainly be room for difference of opinion in the country. He said the PPP had always imposed emergency through constitutional and legal means. “In fact, during the 2008–2013 government, when emergency rule was imposed in Balochistan, it was also because of the terrorism situation, and governor’s rule was imposed there against the PPP’s own government. “If the PPP thought only of itself, how would it have removed its own government?“ He said Fazl’s party has also been affected by terrorist attacks, so he hoped the JUI-F chief would criticise the PPP politically as much as he wished, but also condemn the terrorists. Bilawal added that if Fazl made an effort, harmony between the government and the opposition could be achieved.

items.title: 17e édition de la Journée du fonio : le pari du consommer local à Kédougou
items.description: La 17e édition de la Journée internationale du fonio et de la souveraineté alimentaire se tiendra les 13 et 14 novembre 2026 à Kédougou. L'annonce a été faite dimanche, par le comité d'organisation. Organisée par la Coopérative régionale des acteurs de la filière fonio, elle sera placée sous le thème : « Le fonio du Sénégal : produire, transformer et consommer local pour notre souveraineté alimentaire ». Producteurs, transformateurs, chercheurs, investisseurs et décideurs publics sont attendus à cette rencontre. Des panels, une exposition-foire, des démonstrations techniques et des dégustations culinaires sont prévus pour promouvoir cette céréale traditionnelle. Selon Abdoulaye Diallo, membre du comité d’organisation, cette journée constitue une opportunité pour Kédougou et le Sénégal. Il souligne la nécessité de mobiliser les forces vives de la région afin de faire de l’événement un rendez-vous de référence, au-delà des frontières nationales. Il a également rendu hommage à Aïssata Aya Ndiaye, considérée comme la fondatrice de cette initiative. Au-delà de la célébration, les organisateurs veulent promouvoir les innovations techniques, encourager les investissements et favoriser la mécanisation de la production ainsi que la modernisation de la transformation du fonio. Les organisateurs veulent valoriser le fonio, encourager les investissements, promouvoir la mécanisation et moderniser sa transformation afin d’améliorer les revenus des acteurs de la filière. Fonio: à Kédougou, les femmes misent sur le consommer local La Guinée, le Mali et le Burkina Faso figurent parmi les pays voisins dont la participation est envisagée, confirmant la dimension sous-régionale de l’événement. Les femmes, très présentes dans la transformation et la commercialisation, occupent une place centrale dans cette dynamique. Ndeye Mayata Diop, membre du comité d’organisation, plaide pour un accompagnement accru de l’État. Les organisateurs invitent également le président de la République et le ministre de l’Agriculture, annoncé comme parrain, à prendre part aux festivités. À travers cette 17e édition, les acteurs ambitionnent de faire du fonio un levier de souveraineté alimentaire, de création de revenus et de développement économique. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: Bouré en pleine transformation : Boukaria accélère sa modernisation et affirme ses ambitions administratives
items.description: L’érection de Kintinian en préfecture a marqué le début d’une ère nouvelle pour toute la région. Loin de se laisser distancer, le district de Bouré Boukaria a immédiatement amorcé un virage historique vers la modernisation. Pour répondre pleinement aux critères rigoureux d’une future sous-préfecture, la localité s’est lancée dans une transformation radicale de son paysage urbain et de ses infrastructures. Le changement de visage de Boukaria saute aux yeux dès l’entrée de la localité. Les routes principales sont réhabilitées et reprofilées pour fluidifier le trafic et désenclaver les secteurs environnants. Pour accompagner cette dynamique, des opérations majeures de déguerpissement des emprises publiques ont été menées. Cette libération des voies permet de redessiner une ville plus ordonnée, aérée et prête à accueillir les édifices publics indispensables à son futur statut administratif. À travers ces chantiers, Boukaria prouve qu’elle ne veut plus seulement être un pôle économique aurifère, mais aussi une entité administrative forte et autonome. Cependant, ce développement tant attendu s’accompagne d’un signal d’alarme que l’on ne peut plus ignorer. Les travaux routiers et le trafic intense soulèvent une couche de poussière suffocante qui est en train d’envahir toutes les localités. Il est de la responsabilité absolue des autorités locales, des comités de développement et des entreprises d’infrastructures de prendre les mesures idoines face à cette urgence sanitaire. Le développement ne peut pas se faire au détriment de la vie des citoyens. Les décideurs doivent impérativement prendre toutes les précautions nécessaires pour préserver la santé des populations face à ce fléau. Cette lutte farouche contre la poussière ne doit pas s’arrêter avec la fin des chantiers : elle doit être une priorité permanente, pendant et après les travaux, dans chaque recoin de Bouré Centre. Bâtir des infrastructures routières est une excellente chose, mais protéger les poumons et la vie des habitants reste le premier devoir de ceux qui nous dirigent. Mamoudou Kéïta, correspondant à Kintinian 628 61 88 90 L’article Bouré en pleine transformation : Boukaria accélère sa modernisation et affirme ses ambitions administratives est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Yagbonwura to attend 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival in Anloga
items.description: The Overlord of the Gonja Kingdom, Yagbonwura Bii-Kunuto Jewu Soale I, will make a historic visit to Anloga in the Volta Region on November 7, 2026, to attend this year’s Hogbetsotso Za. He is expected to deliver a speech at the grand durbar as the Guest of Honour. His participation is expected to strengthen cultural ties between the Gonja and Anlo people and deepen cooperation between the two traditional areas. A delegation led by Togbui Amey Zegu II, on behalf of the Awoamefia of Anlo Dukor, Togbi Sri III, extended the invitation to the Yagbonwura at the Jakpa Palace in Damongo last Friday. This year’s celebration is on the theme, “Anlo, Our Heritage and Our Values: Striving to Build One Ghana for a Better Tomorrow.” The Hogbetsotso Za commemorates the Anlo-Ewe people’s migration from Notsie, in present-day Togo, to their current homeland after escaping the rule of King Agorkorli I. Cultural heritage In his remarks, Togbui Zegu II said the festival offered an opportunity for the Anlo people to reflect on the values that had sustained their identity across generations, including unity, resilience, courage, discipline, communal responsibility and respect for tradition. He said the celebration would feature activities designed to attract tourists, support local businesses and deepen community participation. A major highlight will be the sitting-in-state of the Awoamefia and his paramount chiefs, followed by a grand durbar featuring traditional displays by the various states of Anlo Dukor and the participation of national dignitaries. Togbui Zegu II assured the Yagbonwura and his entourage of appropriate protocol and hospitality arrangements during the visit. He also wished the Overlord of the Gonja Kingdom continued success in promoting peace, prosperity and development among the Gonja people and across Ghana. Acceptance For his part, the Yagbonwura accepted the invitation and said the festival was a great opportunity for the two kingdoms to renew their bonds and deepen collaboration. He said the people of Gonjaland and Anlo shared historical ties dating back centuries, adding that the visit would help strengthen their relationship and promote greater cultural understanding.

items.title: Rap battle, more thrills mark final day of Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair in Ho
items.description: The Ho edition of the Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair has come to a close, ending three days of exhibitions, public engagement and activities connecting visitors with businesses in the housing and construction sectors. One of the highlights of the final day on Sunday, October 18, was a rap battle involving some participating institutions, which took turns rapping to a selected beat to introduce their organisations and highlight the products and services they offer. The contest brought a different kind of energy to the grounds, as exhibitors cheered one another on and joined in the excitement. At the end of the competition, Rhoyak Ventures emerged winners, while DoorMasters placed second. The two institutions received souvenirs from some of the exhibitors in recognition of their performances. Beyond the entertainment, visitors continued to make their way to the Ho Sports Stadium to explore the exhibition stands, interact with exhibitors and seek information on products and services related to housing, construction and home improvement. Participating businesses showcased a range of offerings, including building materials, property development, roofing systems, water storage solutions and home security. The fair provided visitors with an opportunity to engage directly with industry players and learn more about available options for their housing needs. The three-day event, which began on Friday, October 16, brought together businesses and members of the public, with cultural entertainment and activities for children also forming part of the experience. With the rap battle providing a lively finish to the final day, the Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair has now concluded its Ho edition, bringing this chapter of the exhibition to a close.

items.title: Drone strikes kill civilians in Darfur and Kordofan as attacks target eastern Sudan
items.description: Drone attacks killed civilians in West Darfur and West Kordofan on Saturday, including women, while further strikes targeted military installations in eastern Sudan. A separate fire destroyed up to 80 commercial stalls in Northern State. In West Darfur, a drone strike attributed to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed several people, including six women, and injured five others in Bir Saliba, in Sarba locality. Sources said most of the victims were displaced people who had travelled to the area to work in agriculture. The Joint Force, allied with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), took control of Bir Saliba in early October, while fighting has continued in surrounding areas. Civilian lorry hit in West Kordofan In West Kordofan, the Kordofan Observatory reported that an SAF drone strike on a civilian lorry near Ankush killed four civilians, including three women, and injured others on Saturday. The vehicle had travelled from Abu Zabad locality, towards El Mazroub in North Kordofan. Civilians were on board, including patients travelling for medical treatment and people heading to the town to shop. The Observatory also reported that a drone attack killed three civilians in Fouja area on Wednesday, while a separate strike on the village of El Janana, near Wad Banda , killed a child the same day. Condemning the attacks, the Observatory said targeting civilians and civilian vehicles violated international humanitarian law and could amount to war crimes. It called on the SAF to stop attacks on civilians in Kordofan and urged the RSF to keep away from residential areas. It also called for the incidents to be documented and those responsible held accountable. Drone attacks target military sites in eastern Sudan Drone attacks targeted military installations in El Gedaref, Khashm El Girba and the Upper Atbara and Setit Dam Complex on Sunday morning, according to eyewitnesses and field reports. Air defences reportedly intercepted several drones, including three targeting the Ali Atbara Dam in El Fashaga locality and another over Khashm El Girba. Two drones targeting El Gedaref were also reportedly shot down. No casualties were reported. Fire destroys up to 80 stalls in Northern State In Northern State, a fire destroyed between 75 and 80 commercial stalls in El Burgeig market on Saturday evening. Resident Shaker Abdelrahim told Radio Dabanga that people heard explosions before the evening prayer and then saw thick smoke rising from the market. The fire swept through stalls packed with goods, destroying their contents. Initial accounts attributed the blaze to an electrical fault inside a shop. Abdelrahim said the concentration of perfume shops helped the flames spread rapidly. items.title: Lassiry Hip-Hop : six artistes guinéens recherchés pour une scène à Paris, La Fouine attendu à Conakry
items.description: La 8e édition du festival Lassiry Hip-Hop se déroulera entre Conakry et Paris, du 29 octobre au 7 novembre 2026. Au-delà des concerts, les organisateurs veulent créer des passerelles entre artistes, universitaires et professionnels de l’industrie culturelle. Un grand concert avec le rappeur français La Fouine est annoncé au stade Petit-Sory de Nongo, avec 10 000 spectateurs attendus. Le festival Lassiry Hip-Hop entend faire du rapprochement entre la Guinée et la France un levier de développement pour les cultures urbaines. Pour la première fois depuis sa création, l’événement porté par Guinée Challenge Afrique franchira les frontières guinéennes avec une programmation à Conakry, du 29 octobre au 1er novembre 2026, puis à Paris, du 4 au 7 novembre, en collaboration avec La Place de France. Les organisateurs ont présenté cette nouvelle orientation le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, au Centre culturel franco-guinéen (CCFG), à Conakry, devant plusieurs acteurs du secteur culturel. L’initiateur du festival, Mbaye Aissatou Fall, a mis en avant la volonté de développer les échanges artistiques, de favoriser la mobilité des professionnels et de multiplier les opportunités de collaboration entre les deux pays. « Pour cette 8e édition, on essaie encore de grandir, d’aller plus loin, très loin encore. Cette 8e édition est une édition très spéciale parce que Lassiry va s’exporter pour la première fois au-delà de notre continent, de notre pays. Donc, Lassiry va se faire en Guinée, à Conakry, et en France, précisément à Paris. On est sur une collaboration entre artistes, sur la mobilité des professionnels et la connexion entre les artistes et les professionnels », a-t-il expliqué. L’ouverture du festival à la scène française constitue une occasion pour les artistes guinéens de gagner en visibilité et de nouer des contacts susceptibles de faire évoluer leur carrière. Dans cette perspective, six artistes seront sélectionnés pour participer aux activités prévues à Paris. Mbaye Aissatou Fall a lancé un appel aux membres de la diaspora guinéenne, notamment aux musiciens vivant en France, afin qu’ils prennent part à cette initiative. Les inscriptions sont ouvertes en ligne, selon les indications données lors de la cérémonie. « À l’endroit de la diaspora, on vient exporter le hip-hop made in Guinée à Paris, ça ne se fera pas sans vous. Et je m’adresserai aux artistes précisément : tu es en France, tu es à Paris, tu fais de la musique, on a une opportunité à t’offrir. Viens nous rejoindre à La Place, on a ouvert des inscriptions en ligne, postule », a-t-il lancé. Les artistes retenus auront notamment l’occasion de présenter leurs créations à des producteurs, des manageurs et des tourneurs présents dans l’environnement professionnel parisien. « On va sélectionner les meilleurs, on va donner l’opportunité à six artistes de s’exprimer à Lassiry, parce que Lassiry, c’est un carrefour de business, là où tout le mouvement hip-hop, les professionnels, les producteurs, les manageurs, les tourneurs se retrouvent chaque jour sur des événements. Donc, viens t’exprimer, avec un temps record pour convaincre un producteur ou un tourneur », a-t-il précisé. L’initiateur a également invité les amateurs de musique à se mobiliser pour les spectacles organisés à Paris, où la salle retenue dispose de 500 places. « Nous sommes sur une salle de 500 places, les tickets, ça part vite. Les Français, ils ont envie de découvrir ce qu’on est en train de faire. Donc, ne te fais pas raconter ça, prends ton ticket et prépare-toi, viens supporter tes frères guinéens », a-t-il déclaré. Le festival ne se limitera pas aux prestations scéniques. Cette édition introduit également le « Lassiry Business Tour », un programme destiné à rapprocher les professionnels de la culture du monde universitaire parisien. À travers des rencontres dans les universités, les organisateurs souhaitent présenter aux étudiants et aux jeunes diplômés les possibilités d’emploi et d’investissement offertes par les industries culturelles et créatives, particulièrement les cultures urbaines. « La nouveauté cette année, ça va commencer par cette mobilité. D’habitude, on invite les gens qui viennent en Guinée, mais cette année, on va quitter la Guinée pour aller à Paris. C’est une nouveauté. Un nouveau concept qui s’appelle “Lassiry Business Tour”. On va aller dans les universités pour parler des opportunités que la culture ou les cultures urbaines offrent aux jeunes diplômés », a indiqué Mbaye Aissatou Fall. Pour lui, la consolidation de l’industrie culturelle nécessite des compétences qui dépassent le seul domaine artistique. Le droit, le commerce et les sciences peuvent notamment contribuer à la gestion des carrières, à la protection des œuvres et à la valorisation économique des créations. «Parce qu’un artiste, c’est une entreprise, c’est une marque déposée. Pour être une entreprise et une marque déposée, il faut être structuré. Pour être structuré, on a besoin de l’intellect, et l’intellect se trouve dans les universités. Donc, on va aller convaincre ces universitaires de nous rejoindre dans la culture, parce que ce n’est pas du fainéantisme, c’est du business qui fait beaucoup d’argent », a-t-il soutenu. Cette démarche vise à encourager les juristes, les diplômés des écoles de commerce et les techniciens issus des filières scientifiques à mettre leur expertise au service des acteurs culturels. Sur le plan artistique, Lassiry Hip-Hop prévoit plusieurs créations communes entre musiciens des deux pays. Selon Mbaye Aissatou Fall, quatre collaborations sont envisagées, avant une prestation collective réunissant les participants. « On aura […] quatre collaborations B2B. […] Un artiste français, un artiste guinéen ; un artiste français, un artiste guinéen ; un artiste français et deux artistes guinéens. Et après, ça va se terminer par une collaboration collective entre tous les artistes là, qu’on va bien structurer, là où tous les artistes vont gagner leurs royalties », a-t-il expliqué. Les organisateurs entendent ainsi faire de ces rencontres un espace de coopération artistique, tout en veillant à ce que les participants puissent bénéficier des revenus issus de leurs œuvres communes. Le festival mettra également à l’honneur plusieurs disciplines des cultures urbaines, notamment le rap, le graffiti et le DJing. La danse figure aussi parmi les activités prévues à Conakry. Évoquant les difficultés liées aux déplacements internationaux et aux procédures de visa, l’initiateur a défendu la vocation universelle de l’expression artistique. « Le monde serait mieux sans visa, mais nous, en tant qu’artistes, cette histoire de visa, c’est dans la tête. On s’exprime pour voyager avec notre passion », a-t-il affirmé. À Conakry, le public est attendu au stade Petit-Sory de Nongo pour un grand concert qui devrait constituer l’un des moments forts de cette édition. Les organisateurs tablent sur une affluence de 10 000 personnes et annoncent la présence du rappeur français La Fouine comme tête d’affiche. «La plus grande nouveauté encore, c’est le grand concert sur le terrain Petit-Sory, là où on attend 10 000 personnes avec, pour la première fois, une tête d’affiche énorme, qui est La Fouine », a annoncé Mbaye Aissatou Fall. Présent lors du lancement, l’artiste et producteur Ablaye Mbaye a félicité l’équipe organisatrice pour les efforts consentis, notamment dans la mise en réseau des acteurs de l’industrie culturelle et créative. Il a également exprimé son soutien au festival. La cérémonie de lancement s’est achevée par des prestations de plusieurs artistes, dont Kamkilambé, Miss Kalakala et Thiird. Avec cette programmation entre Conakry et Paris, Lassiry Hip-Hop ambitionne de renforcer les relations entre les scènes guinéenne et française, de faciliter la circulation des artistes et de promouvoir une industrie culturelle davantage structurée et créatrice d’opportunités professionnelles. Mayi Cissé L’article Lassiry Hip-Hop : six artistes guinéens recherchés pour une scène à Paris, La Fouine attendu à Conakry est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Burkina: 119 commerces contrôlés, 18 mis sous scellés à Dano et à Oronkua
items.description: (Dano, le 18 octobre 2026) Du 13 au 17 octobre 2026, la Direction régionale de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat du Djôrô (DRICA-Djôrô), en collaboration avec la Direction régionale de la Police nationale, a mené une opération de contrôle des produits de grande consommation à Dano et à Oronkua, dans la province du Ioba. Cette opération visait à veiller au respect de la réglementation commerciale et à protéger les consommateurs. Au total, 119 commerces ont été contrôlés. À l’issue des vérifications, 18 établissements ont été mis sous scellés pour diverses infractions, notamment des pratiques de prix illicites, des atteintes à la sécurité des consommateurs et la vente de produits prohibés. L’opération a également permis de retirer du marché environ deux tonnes de produits impropres à la consommation ou prohibés. Les manquements constatés ont fait l’objet de sanctions conformément à la réglementation commerciale en vigueur. À travers cette action, la DRICA-Djôrô réaffirme sa volonté de poursuivre les opérations d’assainissement du marché. Elle invite l’ensemble des acteurs économiques à respecter la réglementation en vigueur afin de contribuer à la protection des consommateurs et à des pratiques commerciales conformes aux textes. DCRP/MICA DRICA-DJÔRÔ L’article Burkina: 119 commerces contrôlés, 18 mis sous scellés à Dano et à Oronkua est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Four soldiers dead, dozens injured in fire at Canada military base
items.description: Four soldiers were killed and dozens injured in a fire at a military base in Alberta province, one of the worst peacetime tragedies to hit Canada’s armed forces on home soil, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Sunday. Carney made the solemn announcement without providing details on what caused the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright on Saturday. “It is with deep sadness that I can confirm, at this time, that four service members have lost their lives and that their loved ones have been notified,” Carney said in the capital Ottawa, adding that “dozens of others have been seriously injured”. “This is one of the worst tragedies the Canadian Armed Forces have experienced on Canadian soil in peacetime,” he said. Canadian Defence Minister David McGuinty said late on Saturday there were “fatalities and injuries” following an incident at a military base in western Canada. “I’m saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base,” McGuinty said. Prime Minister Mark Carney had posted to X earlier on Saturday that “a serious incident creating a major fire” had occurred at the base. Neither offered details on the number of casualties or the nature of the incident at CFB Wainwright, located about 200 kilometres southeast of Edmonton. “We will have more to say in the coming hours and days,” McGuinty said. A doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, about 200 km northwest of the base, told public broadcaster CBC that Wainwright’s health-care facilities were “completely overwhelmed” by the number of patients requiring care. “It is more patients than any of us want to count right now,” Warren Thirsk said. “It’s a disaster. It’s a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster.” According to the Department of National Defence, the fire broke out around 4pm local time on Saturday (3am PKT on Sunday) in the base’s training area. The Municipal District of Wainwright posted on social media that the fire had “spread rapidly due to high winds”. It said later on Saturday that the blaze was “being held at this time”, though firefighting crews would continue to monitor the area. “Military and civilian crews fought this fire throughout the night in some of the worst conditions imaginable, risking their lives to protect their fellow Canadians,” Carney said. The Wainwright base is one of the largest bases operated by the Canadian Armed Forces and it regularly hosts training exercises involving military personnel from Nato countries. “We will care for the injured through every step of their recovery,” Carney said. “And we will stand by the women and men of our armed forces as they bear the weight of this loss, they will not carry it alone because in Canada we take care of one another.” The fire disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday’s vote on whether to begin the process toward a future referendum on Alberta’s independence from Canada. Alberta’s office responsible for overseeing provincial elections said the advance voting station in Wainwright had closed.
